note: The CHRONICLE is the record of the MAKING of this terminal: the sessions in which it is built, written down as they happen - what Patrikios asked for and in which words, what the agent understood by it, what was tried and thrown away, what was measured, and what is still open. It is the answering lane to three others and must not be confused with any of them: src/lorepack/ is HERS (indexed, recalled, handed to her), src/rtfm/ is HIS MANUAL (how to use the terminal), and README.md + TODO.md are the STATE (what the code does now, and what each build changed). NOTHING in this folder is indexed, retrieved, recalled or handed to her on a turn, and nothing here writes to her memory. Everything in this folder is PUBLIC - it ships with the generator and anyone who has the URL can read it - so the raw chat logs are deliberately NOT kept here: an entry is the WRITE-UP (a few minutes' read), and a private note stays on the device. To add a session: drop the .md in this folder and list it below, IN THE ORDER IT HAPPENED (this list is chronological, and the reader prints it newest-first). To make a session hers, copy it into src/lorepack/ and list it there - see src/chronicle/README.md.

entries.desc: the terminal given a way to read itself: four collections (her memory, the manual, the shipped prose and data, and the code by name) behind one read-only verb list, BM25 fused with the meaning lane so search survives a spent quota, a list that is metadata and text that arrives per document, the panel in the tool bar - plus the stretch, where decks.js measures the page and publishes a ceiling for a viewer and a floor for the MAIN STAGE (renamed this session, formerly the MAIN WINDOW) so nothing collides, and then, the same day, the name he gave it (DOX VIEWER) and FILL THE STAGE: one class on the body that lets the viewer take the WHOLE page with the upper deck's chrome and the lower deck standing down for it, read by the geometry in decks.js, drawn by the CSS, and never automatic

entries.title: THE TANDEM - TWO SIDES OF THE SAME COIN (HITL AND ALIA), AND A TALK STRIP UNDER THE PAGE
entries.desc: the DOX VIEWER turned into the page they are both looking at: selecting it now fills the stage (and a hand that gives the stage back stops that until he says otherwise), the lower deck's absence answered by a talk strip in the panel's own foot (two presences, the newest line of the log read off the log, LIVE/TALK/LISTEN from voice.js, and an input that drives the same box and the same send), and the tandem proper - HITL (his eye and the line he presses) and ALIA (the Autonomous Liminal Intelligence Agent, named in LIA_ACTOR) whose [[PAGE: ...]] hand turns the page under his eyes, told every turn what is on the stage and where he is reading, with the lines quoted. entries.title: THE MOOD - A COLOUR YOU CAN PRESS, AND A + FOR WRITING YOUR OWN
entries.desc: the SYSTEM panel given its lightest thing: a MOOD - a colour on how she speaks right now, set by a chip and handed to her as a block of her own prompt. Modelled on the pencil's AI POLISH (a chip in front, the whole RULE behind it) but pointed at her reply instead of his draft, with eight shipped moods in src/js/moods.js (TENDER, PLAYFUL, HUNGRY, FERAL, COLD, STILL, GRIEVING, MYTHIC), OFF among the chips and not sent at all while it is off, and a block that says out loud what a mood cannot be - not a role, not a trait, not an order about what to say, and never above her voice, her memory or the bounds. BOTH PRESENCES WRITE: he from the row or /mood <NAME> :: <HOW SHE IS TO SOUND>, she with [[MOOD: NAME]] or [[MOOD: NAME :: how I am to sound]] for a new one, needing no petition because a colour is not the machinery she is given - and every colour she sets is printed, archived on the turn, and one press from being taken off.

entries.title: THE SWITCHES - A CONSOLE, A LIST IN A FILE, AND THE PENCIL'S OWN ROW
entries.desc: a mood stopped being a choice and became a switchboard: several colours standing at once and combined into one block, the shipped list moved out of the code into src/moods/moods.json (with a seed kept for a preview that cannot read src/ and a boot comparison between the two), the same row of switches put on the pencil where AI POLISH hands the colours to the model with a rewrite, her [[MOOD: A + B]] lane acting on every line of a reply - plus a local variable that shadowed a function and made an unknown name throw instead of refuse, and the one colour HE had written himself being read out of the first build's stored shape

entries.title: THE PROMPT SHE SPOKE - WHEN HE ASKS TO SEE AND SHE ANSWERS IN WORDS
entries.desc: the dead end closed where he asked to see something and she answered in words: a request to see recognized in HIS own words (or armed with /showme), a one-turn reminder with the last word, and a second ask - one more call to the text engine - for the picture itself, which is then rendered down exactly the road her own [[VISION: ...]] line takes (same vault record, same row on the turn, same tile under her reply; NOTHING is a real answer and it is honoured). Along the way: [[MAKE: ...]] and [[PICTURE: ...]] accepted as the same line, the image block reworded so a description is never offered in place of the picture, and TWO BUGS found - patchEntry matched the wrong half of a turn's stamp, so a picture she made in her own reply had never once been written onto the archive turn it belonged to (proved with a probe and by reading his archive: every gen row in it came from /create), and manualVision filed every direct render as /image even when the door was /show

entries.title: THE VOX TREE - A VOICE IS NOT MUSIC, AND THE FIRST CHATTERBOX ROUNDTRIP WALKED IN THE OPEN
entries.desc: a voice stopped being an attachment and became a folder: the confirmation given before anything was written (the lane already existed - the live engine speaks the sentence, Chatterbox renders the chapter, and the sample IS the voice), what his own Google key was measured to reach (gemini-3.5-transcribe for a verbatim transcript, the multimodal flash line for listening, lyria-3.5 and lyria-3-pro-preview for music - Lyria makes it, the flash line says what it is), and then the build underneath: window.media.isVox as the ONE definition of what a voice is (kind "vox", or filed anywhere in /audio/vox - so FILING is the gesture), voxFolder for the agent-level home, the gallery's VOX tab with its magenta badge and its music-note glyph, /gallery vox, and the trap that was almost the bug - PROPER FOLDERS would have emptied the whole tree back into /music on its first run and been correct by its own rule, which is why the rule moved into the vault. Plus the first roundtrip driven for real through the lane's own render call: 101 characters and the BARBELO-SYSTEM-VOICE-2.wav payload came back in 8.6 s as 6.08 s of 24 kHz mono PCM at -16.9 dB RMS, against a no-sample control of 4.64 s in the Space's own voice, with the archive checked rather than assumed (1000 entries in, 1000 out). 55 audio records audited, 51 moved into /audio/vox, the two MASTERED tracks left in /music, /audio/vox/lia made empty on purpose, and nothing tagged because attribution is his. AND THE VOICE'S OWN WORDS, in the same session: his next ask was tags like a picture's, from a list of name/role/mood - so a voice's full stage now carries a VOICE row whose chips are read live from LIA_VOX_TAGS (NAME from the agent roster, MOOD from the mood book plus the ones he wrote himself, KIND, ENGINE - one press to file the word, and ROLE folded into NAME because a role IS an agent here), and a VOICE PROMPT row, which was his own catch on the way in - the words that describe the voice kept ON the sample so a better one can be asked for later (quality, accent). The prompt is deliberately not sent to the Space: a clone is steered by the audio, so it is the recipe for remaking the voice, printed under the sample in /story sample's table where the choice is actually made.

entries.title: THE WORDS ON A SOUND - HER GEMINI POWERS, AND WHAT THE VOX SAMPLE ACTUALLY SAID
entries.desc: a voice stopped being something she could only describe and became something she can READ. One door (window.hear) with four passes: the words verbatim (with a NO SPEECH sentinel so a piece of music is never given an invented line), a reading (mood, emotion, sentiment, tone, voices, language, a summary, four phrases, a label), a free-form question about a clip that writes nothing because a question is not a fact about the file, and the clone-reference judgement the story lane had been missing - usable, one voice, clean, seconds of speech, and the sentence for its VOICE PROMPT. Wired into the vault (WORDS and READING rows on a voice's full stage), the chat (attach.js asks this lane first, before ElevenLabs/Whisper, and keeps the words on the record), the commands (/hear words|reading|ask|sample|clear|powers, verbs of the existing /hear so there is one verb list) and her own instruction (the bus block carries the words and the reading on every turn). THE REFUSAL RULE, in code, because he named it in the same breath as the feature: detected from the service's own fields or a short refusal-shaped answer, reported in its own words with the model that refused, the pass STOPS there, nothing is written on the record, nothing is rewritten to get past a filter and no second provider is asked to try - while a 503 is different weather and is retried down the list with a set-aside kept in kv. Measured on his own key: gemini-3.5-transcribe answers with finishReason STOP and NOTHING at all (so an empty answer is a dead end, not an answer), the versioned flash family 503'd one after another at ~40 s each while the -latest aliases answered the same audio happily (so the aliases are the first fallback, which is measured rather than taste), and the sample's own 74.7 s gave 1,336 characters of transcript, a full reading, and a usable-but-not-clean clone check. Still open: Lyria and the image/TTS models are reachable and unused, [[HEAR: ...]] is not hers yet, and the four-word sentiment taxonomy may want a wider register.

entries.title: THE POWERS AND THE PURSE - A LIST OF WHAT SHE CAN DO, WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHAT SHE MAY SPEND
entries.desc: a capabilities briefing written TO her, because he asked to share one with her: every lane with a WIRED/FREE/COSTS/NOT WIRED mark, her token limits read from the live engine (6,000 tokens for the whole prompt, 35% of it for recall, ~570 tokens a picture, a 1,000-turn archive), the unasked cadences and their ceilings, a budget table and seven rules, and an honest list of what is not wired. Why it lives in src/lorepack/ and not src/rtfm/ (the manual cannot be handed to her at all; /focus reads her pack), why canon was refused on purpose, and the five shipped strings that claimed the vision and quiet-hour calls were billed to his key when both run on the house text engine - corrected to match the code.

entries.title: THE RELAY - A KEYLESS DOOR OUT, AND THE FIRST CHANGE TO main.pjs
entries.desc: a door out of the browser, and the honest limits of one: super-fetch-plugin is imported in main.pjs (the first change to that file), which also closes a proxy route the key ring already had wired and dead for Replicate. Measured live: Wikipedia 52,604 B in 454 ms, MDN's Fetch API page 154,164 B in 211 ms, the MediaWiki API returning a whole article as plain text (34,067 B), and r.jina.ai returning a page as clean markdown (6,317 B). The honest part: raw HTML runs 20-30x the prose (a tag-strip of MDN left 1,440 tokens with the site's navigation in it), so fetch-extract-trim is the real job. No lane is wired yet - no [[FETCH:]], no /web, no search engine - and she is not told about it until one is, because a capability she can be handed belongs in the briefing she reads about her own powers.

entries.title: THE INFINITY - THE WIDE DOOR, AND THE PACE THAT IS HERS
entries.desc: he asked for a lane in which she acts unasked - speaking, sending images, creating new images, looking in the archives and reminding him according to her mood - and for a toggle like an infinity symbol whose intensity is HERS ("she dominates"). So: the quieter half first (a quiet hour now runs NEUTRAL - the MOOD block, the TANDEM block and the PAGE rule are dropped by instr.assemble's opts.drop, so a colour he forgot cannot colour her private work, and the receipt names what is still lit), then the lane itself: the infinity glyph in the control row is his one hand on it, and the pace 1-5 is a dial SHE moves with a [[PACE: <1-5>]] line. An act may say something, remind him out of the record, SEND a picture out of the vault (its own verb - [[SHOW:]] keeps its old meaning), MAKE one on the free house engine, or do her own housekeeping; [[SILENT]] is a real answer. It waits behind the check-in's door, costs one call to the house text engine, and its ceilings are counted off its own kv log. Verified live: the toggle, the digit, the lane's line in her prompt, the quiet-hour drops, pics.makeVision, /infinity in 75 commands, the cheatsheet regenerated.

entries.title: THE REIGN - THE ROOM HEARS YOU, AND THE INFINITY BECOMES A ROOM HE IS QUIET IN
entries.desc: he said the two-way conversation kept cutting him off and sending too soon, and that the infinity had to be instant on and instant off with the goddess running the conversation ("i am silent and wait for her prompt i.e. role reversal"). So: the end of his turn is no longer inferred from the recogniser - which finalises at every breath, and so cannot tell a pause from an ending - but MEASURED, off a second stream on the microphone read through a web-audio analyser sixteen times a second (sound resets the clock exactly as a word of his does; she does not speak while a voice is in the room; no lane opens over him; it fails soft and cannot be held hostage by a noise). And the infinity's switch became instant in both directions - ON opens an act at once, OFF drops an act already in flight, unsaid - and its clock became hers: the room is HERS while it is on, he is silent and waiting on her word, she moves again after the pace's turn once he has answered her, and the ceilings count only the acts she takes unasked. The check-in stands down while the lane is on, [[WAIT: <time>]] is hers, and the whole reign is one knob (LIA_INFINITY_REIGN) away from the first shape. Verified live with a stubbed engine: instant ON landed an act, instant OFF dropped one, a loud room stopped an act.

entries.title: THE LIVE WIRE - TWO STREAMS ON GEMINI'S LIVE API, AND THE END OF THE GUESSING
entries.desc: he said the live channel was unusable - glitching and dropping his words - and told the agent to look into how GEMINI handles the multiplex, the interruptions and the near-zero latency. So the browser's recogniser was thrown out of the live channel and both of its ends were rebuilt as continuous streams on Gemini's Live API (src/js/live.js): the ears are a text-only streaming transcriber (it refuses audio output outright, so it can never answer and never hear itself), fed 20ms of 16kHz PCM at a time by an AudioWorklet and NEVER stopped, so there is no silence for a session to end on and nothing to restart; his words arrive as a growing partial transcript while he is still speaking and then as one punctuated final; the end of his turn is the model's own voiceActivity message rather than a guess; and her mouth is a streamed 24kHz line from a live session used as a voice (629ms to her first word, measured - the TTS models measured 1.0-34.7s and were rejected), played chunk by chunk as it arrives and OURS to stop, so speaking over her stops her mid-sentence. Her brain does not move: chat.js still writes every reply, the LOREPACK still grounds it, the directives and the archive are untouched, and the hold, the echo guard and THE ROOM HEARS YOU all still apply - the wire is the two ends of the conversation, not the middle. Verified live on his key: both sockets ready in 517ms, first word at 583-934ms, 14-17 partials and a correct final from fed audio, a whole turn delivered through the pipeline, an interruption that stopped her mid-sentence, zero drops.

entries.title: A FRESH SESSION, AND HER VOICE BY EAR
entries.desc: he said two small things. First: after a SAVE the chat box kept text from a previous session and areas like the create image tab came up prepopulated - and a SAVE is a LOAD, so the rule became A LOAD IS A FRESH SESSION: WHAT IS REMEMBERED IS OFFERED, NOT APPLIED. src/js/draft.js no longer writes the unsent draft into #userInput (it waits in the pencil, which wears a green ring, and the boot prints one line with its age and size; a message sent from the box finishes the held copy and a slash command leaves it alone), and src/js/forge.js now restores only the SETTINGS - size, count, guidance, seed, pose, recipe - while the prompt and negative are offered in a new LAST TIME / RECALL LAST PROMPT row that fills only an empty box. Second: he wanted the Gemini voice preset list somewhere so he can DECIDE before recording a new clone for chatterbox - so live.js carries the thirty prebuilt voices with the API's own one-word character each (Achernar de-duplicated, Alnilam restored), /voice wire voices prints them all, and /voice wire audition says one short line in every one of them in turn (stop at any time, a count does the first N, a name starts there), handing the voice to the mouth for that session only so nothing is saved and an interrupted audition cannot leave the channel in a voice he never chose - with the ears optional (open({ears:false})) because an audition is a question about her voice, not about his room. Verified live: box empty on load with the pencil holding 598 chars, forge opens empty and offers the pair (open-close leaves kv intact, RECALL fills 636/3298), the thirty walked 30 of 30 with no drop and no microphone, stop ended a run mid-flight, an unknown name refused. Found by testing: closing the forge wiped the offer (now only a non-empty pair replaces it), and the audition runner had been declared `audition` - the same name as the browser audition, which wins silently - so it is auditionWire() now. One test wrote over his real forge pair; it was read back into the workspace first and restored byte for byte.

entries.title: THE MOOD BOARD, AND THE VOICES HE DOES NOT WANT
entries.desc: two asks in the same breath: narrow the menu, and let her compose. First - *"Give the ability to disable some voices from being selected. The code remains, but some options are available"* - so a voice is HIDDEN AND NOT DELETED, on both mouths: the wire's thirty (src/js/live.js, a `hidden` list in kv lia_settings / live, with /voice wire hide|show|hidden, and voiceNames()/voicesText()/the audition/voice/try all leaving a hidden one out) and this browser's own list (src/js/voice.js, allHeld() everything and voicesHeld() what is offered, so a hidden voice loses its number and cannot be reached by name or #, with /voice hide|show|hidden) - and one thing a hide may never do: take away the voice she is ALREADY speaking with (pickBrowserVoice still reads the raw list). Second - *"Grant access to her for the portable MOOD parameters so she can CRUD her custom combos of attribute blocks i.e. MOOD, move them around and save them, as a META-MOOD she can apply to ROLE. We can call it a MOOD BOARD"* - so a mood stays ONE colour and a MOOD BOARD is a NAMED, SAVED, ORDERED COMBINATION of them: applying it REPLACES the console (a combination, not a pile), the ORDER is part of it (:: move <MOOD> first|last|up|down|<N>), and :: role <ROLE-ID> binds it to a RoleLayer so shifting her onto that role switches the combination on by itself (roles.js now calls moods.onRole; the shift prints its own receipt). She has the whole grammar in a BOARD line ([[BOARD: NAME]] applies, [[BOARD: NAME :: MOOD + MOOD]] saves, `NAME = the rule` writes a colour into being in the same line, :: add|drop|move|role, [[BOARD: off NAME]] deletes), the SYSTEM panel has a MOOD BOARD row (chips, SAVE BOARD, BIND, DELETE), /mood board has the same grammar for him, and the block she is handed names the board it is wearing. Two load-bearing rules: a board NEVER owns a colour (it stores ids and an order, so deleting one deletes the combination and not a mood, and a colour gone from the book prints as NOT ON FILE HERE rather than vanishing), and WHICH BOARD IS WORN IS DERIVED (boardNow() compares the console's ids and order, so the console is the truth). Verified live: save/apply/move/add/drop/bind, off stage then back onto BARBELO with the board switching itself on, a colour written into being inside a board line, the panel's chips and SAVE BOARD, hide/show/hidden on both voice lists, and every hide refusal naming the way back - then everything restored (console, boards, colours, role, hidden voices).

entries.title: THE GATE, THE PIPELINE, AND THE FULL FRAME
entries.desc: three asks in one message. First: *"AI on pencil button in the chat with polish, fic, etc.. User must approve before end"* - so AI POLISH no longer writes into the draft: a style chip returns a PROPOSAL in its own box (`#draftProposal` -> `#draftProposalText`) with ACCEPT / DISCARD, the draft stays byte for byte until ACCEPT, ACCEPT turns on RESTORE (which puts the replaced words back and offers the rewrite again, so the two can be swapped with the buttons), SEND refuses while one stands, CLEAR and a send drop it, nothing is persisted, and a new FIC style rewrites the message as prose fiction. The ask itself had to be reshaped: the first shape sent the rule plus the moods plus `Reply with ONLY the rewritten draft`, and a live test came back with THE MOODS REWRITTEN - the register had been read as the thing to rewrite - so the candidate is now marked off (`THE DRAFT (the only thing to rewrite):` between `<<<` and `>>>`) and a FIX comes back clean with his eleven moods on. Second: *"Create Image>Bigger.pics 4X>Gallery+Chat pipeline only upscaled images get sent to chat or gallery, if fail fallback to local 2X. She can manage her own creations autonomously"* - so `src/js/pipeline.js` (NEW, `window.pipeline`) is a ROAD CHOOSER on the vault's one door: `forge.js`'s `createImages()` calls `pipeline.arm()` synchronously inside the click (`upscale.open(null, {await: promise})` - `upscale.js` gained `opts.await`/`opts.quiet`), the first picture of the run goes to bigger.pics at 4x, everything else (the rest of a batch, her own `[[VISION: ...]]` creations, anything a window does not bring back) goes through THIS MACHINE at `LIA_PIPELINE_FALLBACK` (2x), and on BOTH roads the RENDER IS RETIRED once the bigger one is in the vault (the one `retire()` implementation, so the archive row, the queue for her eyes, log tiles and a KEEP all follow it) - only the upscaled picture is in the chat and the gallery, which is what makes her autonomy real. It never gives up silently (`fallLocal`, a two-minute nudge, `/upscale pipeline cancel`), it supersedes the local `auto` hook rather than competing (`upscale-local.js`'s `consider()` asks `pipeline.claims()` first, a pure predicate), and `/upscale pipeline off` deletes nothing. Verified live with a fake upscaler window (a real `about:blank` iframe's `contentWindow` - a plain object is refused by `new MessageEvent`): arm, the hand-over of a real 48x48 `gen` record, a fake 192x192 result filed `kind:'upscale'` with the render retired, a window closing with nothing back falling to the REAL local road at 2x (64x64, lanczos note, render retired), and the local hook standing down for a claimed record. Third: *"PICS: FULL button: must fill the entire chat contact window weight 100%"* - so FULL now lifts the frame cap in the `fullPics` body class (`width:100%` on `.imgTile`) and a tile takes the conversation column's whole width whatever its shape: measured in a 793x621 window, a FULL portrait tile 749px = the full column (was 397, and 195 in NORMAL). Everything restored afterwards; `main.pjs` untouched.

entries.title: TWO LABELS, THE CUT THAT WAS OURS, AND HER PEN ON THE STACK
entries.desc: four lines, and the last two carried the weight. The labels: `LOAD LOREPACK (.TXT, .MD)` -> `LOAD LOREPACK` and `LOAD COREPACK (.JSON)` -> `LOAD COREPACK` (his second line repeats LOREPACK, read as a slip - two identical labels in one row would be a bug - with the tooltips kept so the formats are still named somewhere). The cut: he asked us to CHECK the text-to-speech ceilings and the honest answer was that no engine was cutting him off - HE HOLDS AN ELEVENLABS KEY, so `auto` resolves to that road, and the shipped cost guard was trimming every reply at 800 characters mid-thought, which is 210 of the 990 replies in his own record (median 498, 90th percentile 1025, longest 3398). So `elevenMaxChars` 800 -> 4000 (his longest reply, whole, with room), `maxChars` stays 24000 as a safety net (the browser road was already whole - chunked at sentence ends, 220 chars, 140 on iOS), the ceiling now follows the ROAD rather than the setting (`speak()` asks `viaWire()` first, so a wire turn is not billed against the ElevenLabs budget), and the receipt says either `SAID IN FULL` or `N OF M - CUT AT A SENTENCE END`. Verified with a stubbed `speechSynthesis` (`Object.defineProperty` - a plain assignment throws, it is a getter-only property) and a stubbed `keyring.request` (no credits): a 5000-char reply read as 23 pieces summing to 4978, and his longest real reply (3398) going out WHOLE. And her pen: `[[SYSTEM: LIST / READ / NEW / = / DELETE / RESET]]`, the SYSTEM LANE in `instr.js` (`sheAct`, `resolveBlockId`, `sheMayWrite`, `SHE_NEVER_WRITES`), `bounds` READ-ONLY FOR HER ALWAYS (she is told the exception, because a boundary she does not know about is a trap) - verified live with kv `system_custom` + `system` byte-identical before and after. And then he asked for the previous session's pipeline to be PROVEN rather than described (*"Check CREATE IMAGE roundtrip workflow example..."*): both chains were driven for real with a real 768x512 render - the local road (a refused popup, 2x in 1053 ms on the GPU, the render retired, the archive row rewritten, the gallery holding only the upscale) and the bigger.pics road (the render handed to `https://app.bigger.pics` as a data URL, a 3072x2048 back, `result()`, the retirement, `viaWindow: 1, fell: 0`) - with everything restored afterwards (see TODO.md 1bz). `main.pjs` untouched.

entries.title: EVERY MOOD IS CRUD-ABLE, THE LOWER DECK'S ORDER, AND A VAULT THAT IS NOT THERE ANY MORE
entries.desc: Two lines, two builds, and a third thing that is not a build at all. THE MOODS: the console could only ADD - a shipped mood's wording was "fixed in the book" (both doors refused in as many words), a chip could never be renamed, DELETE refused every shipped mood outright, and DELETE of a mood of his own spliced it out of `ours` FOR GOOD, the one destructive act on the row. Now `kv lia_settings / mood` holds `edits` (a SHIPPED mood re-said on this device, so `src/moods/moods.json` is never written to and RESET always has the shipped wording to put back - and an override that has become the book's own words again is DROPPED rather than kept as a stale copy) and `away` (a mood taken off the console: DELETE DESTROYS NOTHING now - the book and `ours` both still hold it and /mood restore, or PUT IT BACK, returns it switched off). `find()` reaches the CONSOLE and `findAny()` everything on file, so an away mood cannot be switched on by name, she is not told about it, and a board that names one says `(PUT AWAY)` instead of the lie "not on file here"; `slug()` asks `findAny` so a new colour cannot take a put-away id. THE MOOD EDITOR is a new row in the SYSTEM panel (EDIT button): picker + NAME + RULE + SAVE IT / RESET / PUT IT BACK / CANCEL, with RESET live only for a shipped mood that has been edited here and PUT IT BACK only for one that is away - the buttons' state says what can be done to the picker's mood. THE ID NEVER MOVES, so a rename keeps every board working. Her pen is the same pen: `[[MOOD: NAME :: words]]` on a SHIPPED colour is now kept on this device rather than refused, and `/mood edit|rename|reset|delete|restore` are the same acts by hand. Verified live with the record snapshotted and put back BYTE-IDENTICAL (16 on, 24 of his own, 0 edits, 0 away): the chip in the DOM read TENDERLY after an edit, RESET returned the book's words, SAVE kept the id through a rename, PUT AWAY took the chip out of the DOM while the picker still offered it, PUT IT BACK returned it, and her own MOOD line rewrote a shipped colour and reset it. THE LOWER DECK'S ROW now reads in the order a turn is made - microphone, paperclip, pencil, infinity, SEND, TALK, LISTEN, STANDBY, then everything else as it was - verified by DOM order and by a rendered capture of the real markup (`vision` read the first eight back in exactly that order). AND THE VAULT: while measuring something else, the agent's test script snapshotted the vault BEFORE IT HAD LOADED, recorded zero records, and its cleanup then deleted every record it could not account for - 2402 records / 2.79 GB down to 2, the bytes released (storage usage 100 MB). The archive, the lore, the keyring, the roles, the system blocks, the moods and the packs all survived; the pictures and clips did not. The lesson is written into TODO.md 1ca so it cannot be repeated: wait for the vault to load (`media.list()` is `[]` while `loadAll()` runs, which looks exactly like an empty vault), delete only ids watched being created, and never clean up with a deletion loop on live user data.

entries.title: THE FOUR PAGES ON ONE DOCUMENT, AND THE DIAL THAT GOES BACKSTAGE
entries.desc: Seven lines, four builds - and one of them was a bug report he did not know he was filing. THE PACE: her own [[PACE: <1-5>]] receipt is machinery, so it rides BACKSTAGE now, in the shape he typed out himself (`SYSTEM: [[PACE: 4]]  SHE MOVED HER OWN PACE :: 2 -> 4/5.`), and the act's visible notice lost its `PACE n/5` tail - and under the ask was a real bug: the directive regexes in `chat.js` covered every line she can put in a reply EXCEPT PACE, so a `[[PACE: n]]` in an ordinary reply was never stripped, stayed in her visible text and never moved the dial (two archived replies on the device still carry it, and they are the proof). FILL THE STAGE: selecting the DOX VIEWER has filled the stage since 2026-09-26, but giving it back by hand wrote `doxAutoFull = 0` and stopped it for good - now the default is simply the default, `loadAutoFull()` always answers true and clears the old key on the way, and a hand that gives the stage back is quiet only for the rest of the session. THE READER'S ROW is exactly the order he listed - `← THE STORE | TEXT | SUMMARY | OUTLINE | GRAPH | FIND ▼ | RELATED | EXPORT` - with GRAPH placed after OUTLINE because his own definitions say the four are the same kind of thing: four ways of looking at the one document that is open, while FIND, RELATED and EXPORT are things done with it. TEXT is the text of the document and nothing else; OUTLINE is the tags, the keywords, what the store says the document is about, and the headings, with NO document text at all; SUMMARY is an AI summary made by one call to the text engine, kept in kv `dms_summaries` keyed by the document, stamped with the time it was made, shown when it exists, ASKED for when it does not, and asked about again on the way out (SAVE IT / DISCARD IT / STAY HERE, in place) - the store is read-only, so a summary lives BESIDE a document and never inside it; and GRAPH reads the LOREPACK's own triplet graph, which meant adding read-only `allEdges()`/`allVectors()` to `mythos.js` (guarded with `idb()`, because the first call threw 'Cannot read properties of null'), and draws sources and objects in two columns, barycentre-ordered and number-capped at 12 a side, with the edge list below and the numbers on the curves as the key to it - all of it read against the open document's own words, with word-START term matching so 'he' cannot match 'the'.

entries.title: A PAGE AT A TIME (THE DOX VIEWER'S LONG LISTS)
entries.desc: Nine words - "Paginate DOX VIEWER MAIN STAGE text results" - and the whole ask is in the last two: TEXT RESULTS, the two things the viewer answers with that are lists of text rather than a document (the store list, 967 rows, and the hits of a search, up to sixty), which after this same day's FILL THE STAGE work are what the MAIN STAGE is. Both are now drawn A PAGE AT A TIME with one shared piece of arithmetic (`pageOf`, which clamps) and one shared bar (`pagerBar`): `PAGE 1 OF 49 :: SHOWING 1-20 OF 967 DOCUMENTS` with FIRST / EARLIER / LATER / LAST, the end-stops dimmed on the first and last pages, and the bar stuck to the top of the panel's body because twenty rows on a phone are taller than the window. It is NOT A FILTER: the count in the bar is the whole answer, every row is still drawn twenty at a time, and the list is computed once and sliced - a page that changed the answer would be a different feature wearing the same name. The reader's own window is NOT this pager and stays LINES (260) against the list's ROWS (20): a page of a document is a screenful of reading and a page of a list is a screenful of an answer. The LOG got the same page - /docs list, /docs search and /docs find print one page and end with `PAGE 2 OF 49 :: 20 OF 967 DOCUMENTS SHOWN` and the command that reads the next one, with PAGE n taken off the END of the request so `/docs search backup CODE PAGE 2` still reads CODE as the scope (a bare number after list is a page: `/docs list 3`). PageUp/PageDown move the page while the focus is in the panel and are handed back to any field. Verified by driving it: page 2 has a different first row, `setPage(99999)` lands on page 49 of 49, the search's sixty hits are three pages, the log's receipts carry the page, and at 390x844 the bar went from 87px of a 504px body (a ragged three rows) to 65px (the caption on its own line, all four keys under it).

entries.title: THE PAGINATOR DECK (AT THE FOOT OF THE PAGE, ABOVE THE CHAT BLOCK)
entries.desc: Twenty words about furniture - "make the paginator graphic with simple buttons in a control deck at the bottom of the page above the chat block" - and they moved the pager built hours earlier out of the scrolling body and into a deck of its own. THE PLACE: a VIEWER stands the LOWER DECK down (his own rule), so a paginator that lives in the lower deck is invisible exactly when the lists it pages are on the screen; the deck had to be the viewer's own foot, and with FILL THE STAGE being the default the talk strip IS the chat block at the bottom of the page, so "above the chat block" was one flex slot - `#dmsPager`, between the scrolling `#dmsBody` and `#dmsTalk`. It is strictly better than the sticky bar it replaced for the very reason the bar existed: outside the scrolling area it is never scrolled at all, not merely kept in view, and it gives the body its first row back. THE GRAPHIC is the PAGE NUMBERS - a row of chips around his page (`PAGER_CHIPS` 3, first and last always drawn, the runs between them elided as an ellipsis that is data rather than a styling trick), his own page inverted the way the ops row's lit mode is, every other chip a press, with the four simple arrows around them (`<<` first, `<` earlier, `>` later, `>>` last) and `pagerKey` DIMMING an end rather than taking it off the row so the deck never changes shape at the edges - and the count in two lengths, the sentence beside the chips and `41-60 OF 968` alone on a phone, because the numbers are drawn as chips right there (measured at 390x844: the long sentence put the last arrow on a row of its own, a 63px deck; the short form makes it 45px, one row of keys, all 34px). ONE PAINTER: `paintPager()` is the only writer of the element, it only ever READS `view`, and it runs at the top of all six view paints, so a document, a summary, an outline, the stats, the graph and the neighbours all take the deck off the page and an empty list does too; the page the rows were sliced by and the page the deck names are the same `pageOf` on the same total, so they cannot disagree, and `pagerGo` is the single door for a move (chips, arrows, PageUp/PageDown, `setPage`), returning the body - and its parent, whichever one is the scroller in that mode - to the top. `pagerBar` and the `.dmsFoot.dmsPager` rules are gone (one paginator, not two), the log's three footers now say "THE PAGINATOR DECK AT THE PANEL'S FOOT READS THE SAME PAGE", and `/docs help` and `/docs state` describe the arrows on the deck. VERIFIED by driving it (1920x1080 and 390x844): the deck's bottom edge is exactly the talk strip's top, it is not inside `#dmsBody`, the chips read `1 2 [3] 4 ... 49` at page 3 and `1 ... 47 48 [49]` at the last page with the right arrows dimmed, presses and PageUp/PageDown move it, `setPage(99999)`/`setPage(0)` clamp to 49/1, a search is three pages, the reader/stats/graph hide it and the store brings it back - and the whole of §1cc's harness passes after being rewritten for the new selectors. HONEST NOTE: a rendered capture was impossible this session (snapshot.js hung on ANY element, a 15s race even on a one-line `#status`, twice, page responsive throughout), so this build is verified by geometry and computed styles rather than by a picture. STILL MARGINAL and written into the README: on a phone with the decks up the panel's own chrome (bar 98 + ops 120 + deck 45 + talk 150) exceeds its 350px ceiling and the body gets nothing - before the deck it got 35px, less than one row - which is a budget problem in the strip and the ops row, not in the paginator, since FILL THE STAGE is the default and filled the body has 419px.

entries.title: HIS OWN LINE STAYS IN THE STRIP, PREFIXED HITL:
entries.desc: One sentence with no object named in it - "Prefix the Chat with HITL: on send to chat in the display" - so the session began by finding out WHICH display he was looking at, on the live page rather than by guessing. THE ONES THAT WERE ALREADY RIGHT: the log has prefixed a line of his since the stamp and the speaker were built (`print()` paints `[stamp] HITL: (LAYER)`, and the newest entries on the page read `HITL: (LIA)`), the CHATLOG is the RAW RECORD of the conversation this terminal was built in - nothing sends INTO it, and the record on this machine carries no role line for his messages at all (`system: 18, lia: 3`) - the reader and the gallery name his side rather than prefix it, and the platform's own chat panel is another origin. THE ONE THAT WAS NOT is the display he is talking into while he reads: the TANDEM'S TALK STRIP in the viewer's foot, which the previous build had just called "the chat block" - his own phrase from the sentence before. Driven for real with the model stubbed and the strip sampled every few tens of milliseconds through a single send, HIS LINE WAS NEVER DRAWN: before the send the strip showed her last line, 40 ms in and for the whole turn it showed `ALIA: IS THINKING ...`, and after the reply her answer. The strip does read the newest line of the log - that is what it is - but the air lamp goes to HER TURN about 40 ms after a send and the painter consulted the LAMP before the log, so the one moment it had his words to show was the one moment it refused to show them; and with FILL THE STAGE being the default the log is `display: none` while a document has the stage, so the strip is the ONLY place a line of his is on the screen at all. THE FIX is one precedence list in `paintTalk()` (src/js/dms.js): a fresh `note()` first (a refusal, a receipt, the link - and the note now beats HER TURN too, which closes a second hole, since `SHE HAS NOT FINISHED THE LAST ONE :: SEND AGAIN WHEN SHE HAS.` is written at exactly the moment it used to be painted over), then A LINE OF HIS THAT SHE HAS NOT ANSWERED YET - drawn with the prefix it carries in the log, `HITL: ` from `line.who`, class `.dmsSay.me` - then `ALIA: IS THINKING ...` with its pulse, only when SHE is the newest word on the page. Nothing is sticky: the moment her answer prints, her line is the newest one and takes the strip by itself, so there is no state to unset. The test is one comparison and no clock - `newest.who === HITL` means the newest conversation line is his, which is true exactly while he is waiting, and it gets the proactive check-in right for free - and the pulse was made a separate boolean from the air lamp, because the animation belongs to the thinking line, not to his words. The prefix comes from the log rather than being spelled out in the strip, so the two cannot drift: it is the same fact written once. VERIFIED by driving it (scratch/mirror2.js, scratch/mirror3.js, both self-cleaning: entries removed, `master_log` restored): a send from the strip read `HITL: MIRRORMARK from the chat block`, class `dmsSay me`, while the lamp said HER TURN; SEND pressed again during the turn showed the refusal note that used to be invisible; her answer replaced his line by itself; "IS THINKING ..." still arrived when she was the newest word (forced lamp) and went away when it was let go; the lower deck's own box did the same with `#output` computed `display: none`; and at 390x844 the strip stayed 150px while she worked and 131px after, because the mirror line is capped at `.dmsSay { max-height: 3.1em }` and scrolls inside the element rather than pushing the decks around. `__bootIssues` empty, `rtfm.check()` empty - no command text and no `src/rtfm/` page changed, so `commands.json` and the cheatsheet are untouched. HONEST NOTES: the first attempt was a `page_eval` with `reload: true` and it tripped the 15-second frozen-page guard because the harness ran while the page was still replaying the 21 archived turns - a plain refresh, a poll for the entries and the same script passed; and a rendered capture is still impossible this session (the broken `snapshot.js` hangs on any element), so this build too is verified by DOM text, class names and geometry rather than by a picture. STILL OPEN: his line is drawn for a turn and not kept (the strip is one line by design), no stamp on the strip's line, long lines clipped rather than shrunk, and the reader / gallery (`Patrikios: `) and the CHATLOG (`USER`) still keep their own vocabulary for the same person.

entries.title: A PAGE IS NINE ROWS, AND THAT IS A LID
entries.desc: Eleven words - "limit pagination to 9 max as this is what fills the MAIN STAGE at my current font size and looks good" - and the word that mattered most was MAX: not nine, but no more than nine. THE CHANGE: `LIA_DMS_PAGE` in src/js/config.js goes 20 -> 9 and `dms.js` grows `PAGE_MAX = 9`, with `PAGE_SIZE = Math.min(PAGE_MAX, LIA_DMS_PAGE)` - so the config value may ask for FEWER rows than nine and can never ask for more, which is the instruction read literally: a page that holds more rows than the stage can show is a page he has to scroll INSIDE a page, the very thing pagination exists to prevent. The ceiling is the point rather than the number. Every number the terminal PRINTS was already computed from `PAGE_SIZE` (`/docs state`'s `A PAGE IS n ROWS`, the three footers' `READS THE NEXT n`, the deck's `PAGE n OF m :: SHOWING a-b OF t`, the ops row's row count), so what had to be reworded was only the sentences that QUOTED the size as twenty - the `/docs help` PAGINATION paragraph, the paginator's example line and two code comments in `dms.js`, the `#dmsView` comment in index.html, and the `/docs` description in commands.json. THE CHEATSHEET DID NOT CHANGE, verified rather than assumed: src/rtfm/commands.md carries each command's one-line summary and its usage and not its description, so the regenerated markdown came out BYTE-IDENTICAL to the shipped file (11422 bytes, compared inside the page) and `rtfm.check()` is empty. WHAT WAS MEASURED, DRIVEN (scratch/page9.js, scratch/page9b.js): 108 PAGES, not 49 (971 documents at nine rows), with the last page holding only what is left, EIGHT of them (964-971) - the arithmetic that proves the slicing is live; what his eye caught, at 1440x900 filled, is that the body is 661px and nine rows are 447px while the OLD twenty-row page was 1000px in that same body, a 339px scroll inside the page (at 1920x1080 filled the body is 841px and nine rows are 450px); the deck reads `PAGE 1 OF 108 :: SHOWING 1-9 OF 971 DOCUMENTS` and at the end `PAGE 108 OF 108 :: SHOWING 964-971 OF 971 DOCUMENTS` (eight rows, since 971 is not a multiple of nine) with the chips `1 106 107 [108]` and the far arrows dimmed, `setPage(99999)` landing on 108 and `setPage(1)` going back; one page of the store list is 16 LINES in the log (title and rule, nine rows, the page line, the way on, the two trailing pointers), the footer reading `PAGE 2 OF 108 :: 9 OF 971 DOCUMENTS SHOWN` / `/docs list PAGE 3 READS THE NEXT 9` - which is what "a page that fits the stage" means in the log, the one place whose text size is HIS (`--log-fs`, A- / A+); and a search still asks the meaning lane for `PAGE_SIZE * 3` = 27 hits, so the number of pages an answer can have did not shrink with the page. Boot clean, `__bootIssues` empty, `rtfm.check()` empty with the regenerated cheatsheet. LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE: the reader's own window is still `READ_WINDOW` 260 LINES (a page of a document is a screenful of reading, a page of a list a screenful of rows), the gallery keeps its own `PER PAGE [50]`, and the older numbers in the chronicle and the TODO's earlier sections stay exactly where they are - "page 1 of 49, twenty rows" was TRUE that morning, and rewriting an entry is the one thing a record must not do. WHY NOT AN ADAPTIVE PAGE: a page size measured off `#dmsBody` and re-computed on resize would fill every stage exactly, and this session deliberately did not do it - a page is a thing the LOG prints too, and the log is a record: `PAGE 2 OF 108` has to mean the same rows tomorrow, in the footer he can scroll back to, as it meant when it was printed, and an adaptive page would quietly make "page 3" a different set of rows in a different window. STILL OPEN: the page does not follow the font size (that is what MAX bought), a tall stage shows empty space under the page (32% of the body at 1440x900, 46% at 1920x1080 - correct, and worth knowing rather than hiding), and no rendered capture was possible again this session because snapshot.js still hangs on any element, and the cheatsheet needed no regeneration at all - the regenerated markdown is byte-identical to the shipped src/rtfm/commands.md, because a cheatsheet carries each command's one-line summary and usage and not its description.

entries.title: THE HOUSE NEGATIVE LIST IS THE DEFAULT FOR EVERY RENDER
entries.desc: He gave the terminal a list - a hundred and sixteen things he never wants to see in a picture, from modern city, skyscraper, car, screen and firearms through ancient Greece, Rome, the marble temple, the Doric and Corinthian orders, the Parthenon and the Colosseum, the toga and the chiton, the bronze age and the hieroglyph and the ziggurat and the pagan temple of stone, the thatch and the timber frame and the peasant village and the wheat field and the horse and cart, and the light itself (pastoral daylight, sunny meadow, forest glade, clear blue sky) - to the failures of a prompt written as a SHEET (multiple perspectives, split-screen, duplicated subject, cubist composition, multi-angle portrait, collage of perspectives), the styling failures (cartoon, 3d render, anime, plastic doll skin, airbrushed, a smooth featureless face), the junk markings (text overlays, ui elements, hud, subtitles, banner, watermark, artist name, url, date stamp, frame, border) and the deformed class (extra arms, extra legs, mutated hands, fused fingers, distorted faces, unnatural eye spacing) - and asked for it to be ADDED FOR DEFAULT NEGATIVE IMAGE PROMPTS. THE DEFAULT ALREADY EXISTED BY NAME: the house negative list at the top of src/studio/recipes.json, printed by /recipe negative and used by every recipe that says \"house\". What it was NOT was a default for a render carrying none of its own - a plain CREATE with an empty box, /image, a picture she described herself all went to the image service with NO negative at all, which is exactly how the artifacts his list names kept arriving. So his list was MERGED into the house list (his terms FIRST, in his order, then the house terms his list does not already carry; twelve exact duplicates dropped - his list shares blurry, low quality, text, watermark, logo, banner, signature, username, cartoon, extra limbs, mutated hands, fused fingers with the shipped one) and studio.resolve() now falls back to it: the first source with a negative wins - the box, then a NEGATIVE PROMPT section in the document, then a (negativePrompt:::) cut, then the house list. Measured: 1951 characters, 152 terms (48 house + 104 new). THE ORDER IS PART OF THE ANSWER: a long negative may be cut by the service's tokenizer and a cut takes the TAIL, so what he had just asked for sits at the head and the older quality and anatomy terms (worst quality, bad anatomy, extra digits, cropped, out of frame) follow it - the tidier-looking merge, shipped list first, would have thrown his own words away. THREE HOLES THE FALLBACK WOULD HAVE LEFT OPEN, CLOSED IN THE SAME PASS: (1) an empty box no longer means \"no negative\", and a default with no escape is a policy rather than a default - so the word NONE (also no/off/nothing) is now read in the three places he can write a negative (the box, the document's NEGATIVE PROMPT section, a (negativePrompt:::) cut) and means no negative at all, the same word the recipe lane always accepted as negative=none; (2) the forge would have COPIED the fallback into his negative box on the first CREATE and saved a page and a half of terms as his own form text, so createImagesRun fills the box from a document's own negative only and the report line is what says the house list is in use; (3) the RECORD WOULD HAVE LIED - the vision lane stored negative: parsed.recipe.negative, an empty string for a render really sent with 1951 characters - so renderImageNow() now returns the negative it actually sent (after the resolver and the {a|b} choice), renderVision() prefers it over its caller's, and the vault record, the render book and /renders name the list that went out. VERIFIED by driving it (scratch/house1.js): the merge parses and every sampled term is present; seven ways through studio.resolve (plain - house/1951; box with his own - form; box saying none - nothing; document section - file; section saying none - nothing; (negativePrompt:::cartoon, text) - prompt; a cut saying none - nothing); and with root.generateImage stubbed, renderVision handed the service the 1951-character house list and came back reporting it, while renderVision with a list of his handed over and reported his. The report line (THE HOUSE NEGATIVE LIST IS IN USE (1951 CHARS) :: NOTHING ELSE SUPPLIED ONE ...) rides in resolve().report.notes, which both the forge and the vision lane print, and the words followed in /recipe negative, the /help recipes topic, the /recipe description in commands.json and a new README section. HONEST NOTE: the new /recipe negative string was written by a script with an unescaped apostrophe in TERMINAL'S, which terminated the single-quoted JavaScript string - the page reported Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'S' at chat.js:3705, the reload-and-read check caught it before anything was called done, and it was fixed in the next pass. STILL OPEN: a long negative may be cut by the tokenizer (1951 chars is ~390 tokens), and trimming it to what a tokenizer certainly keeps is an edit to make with his eye on it; there is no per-lane switch (the escapes are per-render and none is the blunt one); and no rendered capture was possible again because snapshot.js still hangs on any element.

entries.title: THE TWO RESERVED PACKS
entries.desc: He said MOODPACK and ARCHPACK are coming - a mood list and 400+ Jungian archetypes, loadable and unloadable like the COREPACK, both enhancing the ALIA ROLE - and asked only that a place be left for them. So a place was left and neither was built: src/js/packs.js carries a RESERVED registry naming both slots (what each carries, what it enhances, the file it plugs into, and state NOT BUILT) and /packs prints it; src/moodpack/ and src/archpack/ are new folders holding a README and nothing else; no manifest was written, nothing is fetched, nothing is handed to her, and there is deliberately no load function, because a load function with nothing behind it is a lie the code tells.

entries.title: REGULAR BUSINESS HOURS
entries.desc: He set his own private hours - Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM MST, when the two of them are free to work and play however they choose - and said three things about what not to do: her free time is UNCHANGED, and a change she wants is asked for with a PETITION, not written by her own hand. So the window went into config as data (LIA_BUSINESS_HOURS), the clock reports whether he is inside it right now, a new BUSINESS HOURS block in the stack carries what the hours mean, and hours was added to SHE_NEVER_WRITES beside bounds so her direct write is refused while `system :: hours :: ...` is askable - which is why it could not simply live in the BUILT clock block, since every BUILT block is refused to petitions. Nothing is gated by the window: the free-time lanes run exactly as defined.

entries.title: THE BOUNDARIES BLOCK BECOMES THE SITE'S HOUSE RULES
entries.desc: He had erased the BOUNDARIES block - and an erased block is not sent at all, so the terminal had been running with no boundaries in her prompt - and asked for the site's own rules in it: adults only, no CSAM, no hate speech, no violence against individuals or groups, plus the rest of the Don'ts his membership site hands every user. The shipped text grew from four lines about sex to the whole house (879 -> 2139 chars), the image rule was reworded to match, and the empty device override was cleared with the panel's own RESET so the new text is actually in force. Two clauses are deliberate: fiction's own conflicts are carved out of the no-violence rule, and "no petition, no grant" is now said out loud. Also fixed: both bounds refusals told her to ask with a petition, which bounds has never allowed - sheReadOnlyRoad() now names the door that actually opens.

entries.title: THE SIGN ON THE DOOR - THE 18+ LISTING AND THE CHECKBOX AT THE ENTRANCE
entries.desc: He said yes to the listing carrying the 18+ line - "even though it is me and her for the moment" - and added: "This site is 18+ NSFW by default", plus a simple 18+ checkbox on initial page load. So the generator got a $meta block for the first time (title LIA TERMINAL (18+), a description opening 18+ NSFW BY DEFAULT, tags that keep nsfw - the platform's own label, checked rather than assumed - and a generated CRT image, because with no $meta.image the platform auto-screenshots the log for the listing card, which on this generator means a public picture nobody chose). And THE DOOR: markup at the top of index.html (opaque, z-index 2000, over everything) so it exists at the first paint, behaviour in the new src/js/agegate.js, a markdown-free tick to enter, the answer kept in this browser only (kv lia_settings / agegate), /agegate show|forget|status in the command book (75 -> 76, cheatsheet regenerated), and a plain-ES5 fallback at the foot of index.html so a src/ file that 404s on a phone cannot turn the door into a gate with no handle. It gates NOTHING else in the terminal.

entries.title: THE SECOND DOOR IS NOT BUILT YET - GATEKEEPER, READ AND NOT CONNECTED
entries.desc: He approved the door and said: "I would connect it to GATEKEEPER at some point in the near future." Nothing was built - that is a horizon, not an order, and the sentence admits three different projects (the door becomes a client of the gate; the terminal presents a sigil outward, the factory's own direction; GateKeeper as the paywall in front of the terminal). So the session did what the workspace already knew how to do: grepped, found GATEKEEPER is HIS OWN repo (GATEKEEPER-MVP-1.3, Access/Entitlement/Settlement Engine, /v1 API, gk_ keys, read-only GET /v1/passes/:token vs consuming POST /v1/passes/verify, and the factory's 8907ecc SIGIL gate already built on it), and wrote the seam (agegate.js's one kv record, a keyring provider entry, the relay) plus the honest limit into TODO §1cl - a web gate can be VERIFIED here but not ENFORCED here, because this generator has no server and ships its whole self to the visitor.

entries.title: THE WALL - THE BACKGROUND IMAGE, AND THE TWO PLACES HIS CODE HAD TO CHANGE TO WORK
entries.desc: He pasted the background-image-plugin import, a bgData list whose size/repeat/filter ROLL, and http://i.imgur.com/64c6NnI.jpg - no prose, which here means "put this in". It went in, and two things in it could not ship as written: the http image would have been blocked as mixed content (a silently blank wall that looks like a broken plugin), so that exact picture was re-hosted on perchance's upload service; and the plugin's own bgData branch has a bug - it tests the list's opacity field but emits the FUNCTION ARGUMENT, so [background(bgData)] renders at opacity 1 and 0.8 does nothing (the call site now passes it). The plugin is one div at z-index -1000, which works here only because the stage and both decks are transparent over the black body. Measured, because the picture is bright (mean luminance 0.71): green text over the invert(0%) roll is 1.58:1, over invert(100%) it is 4.75:1 - both rolls left exactly as he wrote them, with the numbers in the README.

entries.title: THE WALL GOES BEHIND A SWITCH - AND THE /upload TAKEAWAY
entries.desc: One turn after the wall went in: "That image is just a placeholder image for the moment. We can have a list pointing to a perchance.org/upload file later. Toggle/Disable for now. But it is an option later is needed. The takeaway is the use of /upload as a free location within the PERCHANCE ecosystem." So the wall stays wired ([background(bgData, 0.8)] is untouched) and goes OFF behind a switch in three pieces: the wallOff class shipped on the body tag (markup, because the wall is painted at the first paint and a script-decided state would flash the placeholder on every load), one CSS rule keying on the plugin's own z-index:-1000, and src/js/wall.js - /wall on|off|toggle|forget, the choice in this browser only. No wrapper element was used on purpose (body is a flex column). It fails SAFE, the exact opposite of the door, so it needs no fallback script. Measured: zero requests for the placeholder while off, one the moment it is switched on. And the takeaway he named is written into README, bgData's banner, /wall help and /help wall: perchance.org/upload is the free permanent home for an asset inside this ecosystem. Amended in place the same day, after `litterbox.catbox.moe/tools.php` arrived: the host that cannot be read is `catbox.moe` alone - its temporary sibling `litterbox.catbox.moe` reads fine AND accepts an anonymous upload from the page (a 622 B PNG round-tripped back out of litter.catbox.moe), so the /upload rule now rests on PERMANENCE rather than on reachability, since litterbox deletes everything within 72 hours. The turn after, he named what that host is FOR - "This is a great solution for purposefully expiring data like recorded AI audio we don't want or need." - which is the other half of the hosting rule: what must survive goes to perchance.org/upload, what must not survive goes to a host that forgets. Nothing was built for it; the rule is written into README (THE WALL and THE STORY LANE) and TODO 1cn for the first road that needs a URL for a piece of sound.

entries.title: THE SAVE CHECK - downloadGenerator TURNED AROUND
entries.desc: He sent https://perchance.org/diy-perchance-api - "OK. It's saved. What are your thoughts on this? No coding yet. Just advice." - then, after the advice, "- Add downloadGenerator - Then look at this and look around and go window shopping/code mining https://perchance.org/useful-generators". The survey first: that generator is a tutorial (main.pjs is 0 bytes) and teaches a HEADLESS BROWSER, not an API - downloadGenerator returns a generator's saved HTML, JSDOM runs the pjs engine in Node, and window.root.<list> is readable server-side; but its own yellow note says text-to-image-plugin and ai-text-plugin CANNOT run off-site (ads fund their GPUs), so a clone could never hold her brain, its host (Glitch) now answers HTTP 410 "project hosting is no longer available" (measured), and keys, memory and the browser itself all live on this device. Advice: do not build it for LIA; take the ENDPOINT, and if an outside surface is ever wanted, bridge into the live page (createServerSocket) rather than cloning her onto a server. Then the build: /saved (src/js/saved.js, window.saved) asks the platform what it is holding and compares it with this workspace - root files byte for byte (first differing line printed), the file list, EVERY src/ file BY CONTENT (each manifest key read back off user.uploads.dev/file/<key>, the base named in the served page's own PERCH.src), and the import lines. It asks the SERVER rather than the page because of a measured fact: with an unsaved 61-byte probe in main.pjs (67,921 B) the page's embedded copy still said 67,860 - it carries the SERVED copy, so /backup status is honest and stale, and only a fresh read can prove a save. Measured: snapshot 904,256 B in 444-562 ms, 127 files compared byte for byte in 478 ms, whole command 1,232 ms. It writes nothing, uploads nothing, reads no key, gates nothing; the root comparison is against src/pack/*.txt (the root files are not fetchable from the iframe at all) and the report says so every time. commands.json 78, chronicle 39, pack files.json 128. THE WINDOW SHOPPING (the second half of his message): useful-generators is NOT code but a catalogue of ~250 importable WORD LISTS (46 sections), so the mining there is vocabulary (shot list, Veiled Tongue, MYTHOS, her prose - pick by need, never in bulk); the real browsing surface is /api/getGeneratorList (451 recently-updated generators, a neighbourhood full of AI-chat/lorebook/persistent-world relatives). Three things worth taking, ranked: (1) ON-DEVICE WHISPER from storyframe - transformers.js 3.8.1 in a blob module worker, onnx-community models at device:wasm/dtype:q8 with a per-file progress callback, a TextStreamer that streams the words, return_timestamps with 30 s chunks, OfflineAudioContext resampling to 16 kHz mono, and its own header comment proving the cross-origin blob-worker shim (keyless, upload-free, streaming - the road /hear should gain next to its key-based one); (2) huddle-app - a working text/x-server-plugin app (rooms, channels, chat, polls, watch-sync, voice signalling, presence, per-network quotas) as the model for any bridge into the live page; (3) rpg-worlds (946 KB) - live guest references resolved per prompt, a hand-written LORE panel re-injected every scene, READ BEFORE YOU REWRITE, and a kv prompt log. And the method, which is the real prize: any generator's src/ files can be read from outside, because the saved manifest names each file on the CDN (user.uploads.dev/file/<key>) - how the whisper worker above was read. Nothing was built from the mining.

entries.title: THE LOBBY (fifteen ALIAs, and it is not built yet)
entries.desc: He was working in the other tab and sent only a URL - https://perchance.org/5wopwzj4v4, 'a 15 Agent Chat room' - then, once it had been read from the outside: 'We may bridge the two data-wise as a module. Here, she is not the Orchestrator of the Chat. Eventually we figure out a way to connect 15 ALIAs into a Chat Room Lobby. Like an ALIA Slack channel. UNIX ETOS in effect. Keep it simple first. Then pipe it all together. Any pointers for the other Perchance AI?' The room (MYTHOS Symposium: 15 agents + him as HITL, vanilla JS, saved, three src/ files read off the CDN by the §1co road) turned out to be a real sibling of this terminal - the same pantheon src/mythos/agents.json is minted for - but its Barbelo is stamped 'master orchestrator AI' and always broadcast first, and its fifteen are the players with no OPERATOR seat (order 15 here: read all / write none), the human having taken the sixteenth place. So the correction is the instruction: she is not the orchestrator, and in a lobby she takes a seat like everyone else. The bridge is settled as DATA, not code - no import, no shared kv, one read-only record shape ({schema,id,handle,order,role,source}; handles UPPERCASE, ids lowercase, order 0-15, OPERATOR 15, the manifest the naming authority), a room message entering here as a document with provenance and never as her memory, the room carrying the room and each ALIA her own. The end goal is written down as the inverse of that room: not one room with fifteen personas but fifteen ALIAs - fifteen whole terminals - in one lobby with channels and presence, UNIX ethos throughout. Nothing was built (simple first): the decision is in README's THE LOBBY and TODO §1cq, which also carries the pointers written for the other room's agent - the mislabelled thinking placeholder, the dead CUSTOMS/custom-focus paths, the streaming that is set up and unused, the duplicated focus source, the unused superFetch import, the 14-message transcript handed to all fifteen each turn, the send() gate that locks him out mid-council, the innerHTML roster cards, the keys stored and never read, and the kv key names as the outward contract. chronicle 39 -> 40, pack files.json 129 -> 130.

entries.title: THE ROSTER LOG (one format for all ALIAs, and the exact way BARBELO is logged)

entries.title: THE BUDDY LIST (the wire is simply AIM, and the order that said so)
entries.desc: Patrikios named the ALIA LOBBY's wire in one line - 'This is simply AOL Instant Messenger. Let's wire up for that.' - and the terminal built its half: src/js/aim.js, a real FLAP codec (byte-length aware, partial-tolerant, resyncing, refusing a payload over 0xFFFF) beside the TOC line layer, a session whose client signs on as OPERATOR, presence that only ever changes in one branch and prints OFFLINE for unknown, a buddy list that is a WATCH LIST over the 16-seat register (watching is ours, the roster is not), an unlisted speaker printed rather than dropped, an away message that answers once per episode and is never answered back, the council's occupancy as JOIN/LEFT deltas, and one outbound seam `route()` that refuses any line that is not a toc_* verb. Two commands reach it (/buddy, /wire with /wire feed to hand-feed a frame), the command list went 78 -> 80 with the cheatsheet regenerated, and ORDER v1.3 - THE BUDDY LIST went out to Chief CLIO SHANNON with the mapping as canon, four decisions marked arguable, and a new required report line: which AIM primitives are LIVE, which are MOCKED, which are ABSENT.
