Grading it turned up the one finding: her register was normalised to her room's OWN earlier role text, not to the naming authority - settled by fetching the factory's src/agents.ts (13,610 B), which matches src/mythos/agents.json verbatim for orders 0-14 and stamps order 15 NULL upstream. 15 of 16 seats differ (role on 14, revision re-dated on 15, lore_policy read widened to all on eight seats and two authority writes downgraded), and the only exactly-right seat is BARBELO - the one I had handed her a specimen for, which makes it a fault in the issuing rather than the receiving. ORDER v1.4 hands over the file, draws the line (take role/revision/meta/lore_policy; the stamp stays home), corrects my own order v1.2's canon line (id UPPERCASE is the join key; handle Capitalized; lowercase role is the archive grep key), and names the sharp edge of section 1cz: the six-field bridge carries role and nothing else, so a bridge-only room is structurally unable to reconcile its register.

entries.title: BLUF (the bottom line up front, and where the tokens get saved)
entries.desc: He said 'TLDR; Save the token and deploy the BLUF protol- Bottom Line up front.' So it became a protocol rather than a style note: ORDER v1.5 - BLUF went to CLIO, requiring every report to open with the verdict (SHIPPED / NOT SHIPPED / PARTIAL / UNKNOWN) in one line with the AIM line (LIVE / MOCKED / ABSENT) directly under it instead of at the bottom, then what changed, what is open and the save state - and the same rule now governs this side's replies and TODO sections. The scope is written into the rule deliberately: BLUF governs ORDER, not completeness, because a short report that drops a receipt is worse than a long one; what gets short is the traffic a human must read before he can decide, while the record (receipts, strings, counts, bytes, the register, the room log) stays whole. It is the first pass of the session with nothing to report as gone wrong: no code changed.

entries.title: THE TRANSMISSION (the chatlog lane, ported and sent to the record)
entries.desc: He said 'Transmit complete chat log code and specs for CLIO', so the terminal's own record-keeping lane was PORTED - not handed over - and sent: chatlog.js (38,555 chars / 38,560 bytes of modern JS, one file, root.kv only) hosted at a permanent URL, carrying put (the import and its seam), capture() (reading the room's OWN panel, the half a room gets for free and the terminal cannot have), brief/status/show/turn/turns/grep/export, the policy pair, origin, wipe and setSpeakers, all obeying the six laws its header states. It keeps the SAME shapes as this terminal's 94,910-byte ES5 chatlog - the same kv key names, the same 200,000-character chunk, the same turn marks, the same join stamp, the same sidecar - so the two rooms' records are one shape and the lobby's history can be assembled later without a translator. CHATLOG.SPEC.v1.md (13,517 chars) carries the laws, the shapes, the API, the measured growth numbers, the five lanes that must not merge, and a 31-check acceptance suite she must reproduce. Proved by loading the port into the live page over the top of the terminal's own window.chatlog (original kept and restored, and pointed at its own kv folder so the real 3.68M-character record was never touched) and running all 31 checks - which caught three real defects before sending: a whitelist of speaker words that missed an agent's own handle, a foreign .json being filed as a transcript instead of refused, and capture() inheriting the import minimum that refused a room's own short panel. The suite was re-run on the exact bytes uploaded and the hosted copy fetched back byte-identical.

entries.title: THE LEGAL PAGES AND THE BUSINESS UNITS (captured, not built)
entries.desc: He sent the membership platform's legal pages into this chat in real time - the content standards, then the Do's and Don'ts, retitled HOUSE RULES, with his method stated plainly: 'I'm just sending you the ideas quickly to get them captured as I think of it in real time.' So nothing was built and the capture is the build: TODO §1de holds the quotes, the token vocabulary and the three findings. Chasing his pointer at perchance.org/i8ixqmhq2p#terms then proved two things at once - both pages ALREADY exist in his own image studio as config-driven modules (src/standards.js + standardspage.js, src/houserules.js + houserulespage.js) with a stable id on every rule, the words in one file and the drawing in another, and the three per-unit values in config.js (operator 'Merk Morassi, LLC', contact '[email]', site 'MYMEMBERSHIPSITENAME.COM'); and that the address he reached for is DEAD - there is no #terms route in that app, only bare-word hashes #standards and #houserules, reached from the foot of every page. The grab also produced a reusable road for reading any generator's src files (parse the inline srcManifest out of the served page at null.perchance.org/<name>, then fetch each path from user.uploads.dev/file/<key>), and two findings worth more than the pages: a substitution token is a MATCH KEY, so a token spelled two ways prints the placeholder instead of the value; and [email] is SQUARE BRACKETS, which in perchance are code - safe in a config string today, evaluated as an expression the moment a token is carried into a templated text node or a .pjs list. Still open and unchanged: the flag icon the REPORT sentence promises does not exist on any surface (the only public area in that studio is the shared shelf, and it has no flag), the real contact address, and the token spelling - settled before more documents are written in it.

entries.title: THE CHATLOG PACKAGE AND THE ROAD INTO A LOREPACK
entries.desc: He said 'Saved.' and then: 'Please package the code for the chat log as you have it now. I need the exact logic and format so we can communicate and save all ALIA's chats for there LOREPACKs.' So the chatlog was packaged - chatlog.js as a BYTE-EXACT copy of src/js/chatlog.js (94,910 B, 1,612 lines, ES5, window.chatlog), CHATLOG.FORMAT.v2.md (16,964 B) with the format written down field by field (kv keys, the 200,000-character chunks and their split rule, the exact meta/history/joins/marks shapes, both sidecar writers and the one the reader refuses, the merge algorithm, the eight laws), and chatlog-to-lorepack.js (14,923 B) - the piece that was missing: how a transcript becomes MEMORY. PART B is two lanes: a document LOREPACK (.txt/.md indexed for retrieval) where a chat enters as a document, and a MYTHOS pack where it enters as one record per turn with a = the ALIA's UPPERCASE id, h = the speaker's handle, vec LEFT TO THE FACTORY (a converter that invented vectors would put meaningless geometry into somebody's memory), a deterministic staging id so a re-ingest is a no-op, and never two ALIAs in one pack. Proved by running it against this terminal's REAL record (3,682,604 chars, 19 chunks: 3,060 KB of turn-per-section document and 3,184 KB of staging JSONL in 225 ms), against both sidecar shapes, against a bare transcript, and by refusing a foreign .json by name - and two defects were caught that way (the refusal named the length gate instead of the real reason; the gate was stricter than the module's). The finding worth carrying: the live record's TURN INDEX IS THIN - turns 24, indexed 'lines', labels [system, lia, you] for 3.68 MB, so meta.turns collapsed from 19,690 to 24 and thinIndex (/chatlog import of a .json sidecar) is the road back, rebuilding the numbering and leaving every word as it is. Also recorded: neither export shape carries per-turn timestamps, so a pack has ts only at export granularity; and one upload trap - text uploads come back as .txt URLs, which a type='module' import refuses, so the .js files were re-uploaded by path. All three hosted copies fetched back byte-identical.

entries.title: THE PACKAGE LANDS - AND THE RECORD IS CUT BACK TO ITSELF
entries.desc: He said 'ACOWLEDGED. Placing code in the uploads for the other agent is the right move, Send the links in my return chat and I send it to CLIO, She does the rest,' so the four links went back as a pasteable block, and CLIO's own session report came back the same day: her room vendored the package into its own src/chatlog/ (module + format + converter, README wired), fetched the hosted copies back (chatlog.js 94,910 B exact, the converter 14,923 B exact), and her /pack <ALIA> emits both lanes in one press - measured on a real room at 200 turns, 9 fields, ids unique, human turns present and labelled HITL, vec null. Her three answers: the thin index stays coarse in HER room (her index is already a per-turn order, so the case belongs to this terminal), human turns DO belong in a pack and ship labelled, and documents come first because they work today with no code while the staging JSONL waits for the factory's embedding step. Nothing was published - a session claim, not a ship. She had flagged the format document's size as a discrepancy rather than ignoring it (17,125 B against the 16,964 B the package report claimed) and read it as a line-ending delta; it is not one - measured on both copies, byte-identical, 293 newlines and ZERO carriage returns: 16,964 is the CHARACTER count and 17,125 is the BYTE count, the document holding 80 three-byte characters and one two-byte character (80x2 + 1 = 161, exactly the difference). And one thing had to be put right on this side: proving the converter against this terminal's REAL record had meant writing three synthetic imports INTO the record (a suite, a bare dump, a foreign json - 1,914 characters with their join stamps), and unlike the earlier round of the same tests this round was not undone, so the live record read chars 3,682,604, turns 24, and a tail of a test string where 'conversation view restored' belongs. It was cut back off and the cut is proved rather than asserted: the clean prefix of exactly the length the record had before the tests (3,680,690 characters) hashes to e291ad08-3829b2 - the fingerprint the record carried after the import of 2026-09-24, and the one written into src/chatlog/manifest.json - so put(..., {mode:'replace'}) wrote it back, and the live record now reads 3,680,690 characters / 3,883,361 bytes / 19 chunks / 69,304 lines / 21 turns / e291ad08-3829b2, tail 'conversation view restored.', with the restore in its own history and the three test turns reading there as imports that were then cut off. The shipped index needed NO edit: it was written for exactly this state, so the restore made it true again. The rule this folder now carries: a test that writes into the record has to be undone in the same pass, and the receipt is the fingerprint - the record is the one artifact here with no undo. Still open: the one click (importing lia-chatlog-20260924-0023.json once through the CHATLOG panel rebuilds the 19,690-turn numbering and changes nothing else - the thinIndex road; a fresh console-script export does the same with the newest turns), per-turn time (console script, never the module), which lane each ALIA's chats go to first, and the mark/id convention at the factory end (d.stagingId). No code in the terminal changed. And CLIO's Player, read against the spec rather than against her report, gave the second half of the session: her staging writer emits v:1 where the factory's own files say v:2, her verify() dimension check reads r.vector after the records were normalised to r.vec (so the mixed-dimension branch can never fire), and the format only IMPLIED the staging shape instead of stating it - which is where the v:1 came from. So the format became v2.1 (a changelog line and B3.1: a staging record is v:2, type:'turn', vec:null, and the factory's embedder owns the transition to type:'vector'), the module and the bridge untouched byte-for-byte, and the format AND the bridge now ship in src/chatlog/ with a package block in manifest.json listing every delivered URL - because a delivered blob is not a source, and a later session could quote that document and not correct it. New delivery, both fetched back byte-identical: the v2.1 document (https://user.uploads.dev/file/be326e8c60d98fccff6c80a0b71808eb.txt, 19,190 B) and a rebuilt zip (https://user.uploads.dev/file/8cabc429d2f40a5dc114ddd5518ba9ab.zip, 43,494 B). Also recorded: a heading is not a handle (both writers head a section '## T<n> - <speaker>' and both readers take the whole heading as the speaker), her kv cache keeps only the first 200 records, and her room now writes TWO pack shapes - the v2 compact staging and the factory's {schema:'MYTHOS.LOREPACK.v1', header, sacred_archive} - the second having no 'a' at all, which is the one field a pack cannot lack because a record whose 'a' disagrees with its pack is retrieved by the wrong agent.

entries.title: THE NEVER-PUBLIC RULE, AND THE ONE BUTTON THAT PUBLISHED
entries.desc: He asked me to mine https://perchance.org/text-to-image-plugin and, of what came back, ruled on one line: '- Do not want this at all as we are never public: The plugin's public gallery'. The plugin was read whole (main.pjs, 37,970 bytes, plus its documentation page) against what this terminal's image lane already does, and most of it had already been arrived at here - the (key:::value) option router with a depth-counted (negativePrompt:::) cut that swallows the rest of the prompt when the bracket is missing (src/js/studio.js does the same thing), one render at a time (the service allows only a few concurrent requests per user), and lazy tile loading (the gallery here is AHEAD: it skips IntersectionObserver entirely and loads by geometry with a safety ticker). Four things were new: removeBackground, which is done CLIENT-SIDE with transformers.js 3.3.3 + briaai/RMBG-1.4 (WASM, imported lazily from jsdelivr, cached on the function) and hands back a transparent PNG - a cutout/sticker recipe waiting to be used, at the cost of one large model download on the user's device; hideGalleryButtons; the plugin's own public gallery (moderated, per-generator, the cheapest public surface on the platform - and the one thing here that PUBLISHES); and the imageTags NSFW API, which only reads images HOSTED by the service, so a local vault is invisible to it and his own prompt-side defence plus the vision classifier is the right shape. Three caveats belong in the manual: a seed is not forever (the plugin's own note: same seed+prompt until the models are upgraded, when the picture a seed refers to changes - which matters to /renders redo R12), referenceImage is DISABLED server-side (2026-08-25, parsed and ignored - no img2img on it), and the ad is already on the page for non-logged-in users with a per-user queue. And one strategic finding: the plugin's first line says do NOT vendor or fork it, and the sanctioned road is a WRAPPER generator that imports the official plugin - which is how his house negative list, pose seed, recipe book, glossary and tag router could reach another room without anybody vendoring anything. THE RULING IS NOW IN CODE, not in a chat message: renderImageNow in src/js/images.js passes hideGalleryButtons: true with every request, set AT THE CHOKE POINT - that function is the only place in the tree that calls root.generateImage (one hit in src/js/) - so the forge, her own visions, /image, a recycle, a batch and every future road inherit it and none can forget it; verified live with root.generateImage stubbed, where the request that went out carried prompt, negativePrompt, guidanceScale, resolution and hideGalleryButtons: true. The promise is said out loud in /help pictures (never uploaded AND never public) and in a src/README.md platform note. Because 'never public' is a claim about a whole lane, the whole lane was walked: the prompt goes to the image service and the text engine; an upscale hands the picture to bigger.pics as a data URL for the session (never published, src/js/upscale.js says so); a voice sample goes to a third-party cloning space once per session (/story sample says so); src/ is public by nature and deliberately kept free of anything private; and NOTHING IS EVER UPLOADED, because no upload plugin is imported - there is no road, not merely no intention. Still open: whether the voice sample is forbidden by the same rule or is the deliberate exception (no sample, no clone) - a decision, not a bug.

entries.title: THE LANE STAYS PRIVATE - THE WRAPPER'S SHAPE, CAPTURED
entries.desc: He asked 'Sketch lia-image-lane as a wrapper, or leave the image lane private? Recommended action?' - after mining the text-to-image plugin had shown that its own first line forbids vendoring it, leaving a wrapper generator that imports the official plugin as the only sanctioned road for sharing this house's image craft with another room. The recommendation was to leave the lane private and NOT build the wrapper yet, capturing its shape instead, and that is what he took: 'leave the lane private now, and don't build the wrapper yet - capture its shape instead, and build it the day a second room actually needs to render.' The reasoning, which is the part worth keeping: a wrapper is cheap, but a second copy of the craft is not - the four tables (house negative list, veiled tongue, pose book, recipe book) in src/studio/ plus the five pieces of logic (studio.resolve, studio.expand, the tag router, the call to root.generateImage, the report) are only half the lane a person actually uses, because the other half is the kv OVERLAYS (pose_book, recipe_book - the poses he has renamed and the recipes he has saved), so a wrapper would carry the shipped half and none of his edits, or carry a copy of the overlays, and the day the two copies disagree the picture is made from a rule he no longer holds - the same drift that cost a day in the chatlog lane this week. And the moment is wrong: every render in the house happens on this page, no second room renders, so a wrapper would be built against an imagined caller with a guessed resolution, glossary, gating and home for the pictures. Nothing is lost by waiting (the plugin is not going anywhere and the craft is already public in src/); what would be lost by not writing the reasoning down is the reasoning itself. So 'src/studio/LANE.md' was written: what a wrapper would carry, item by item with the file each piece lives in today; what must never travel (the vault, her voice, the record, the renders book and the kv overlays - a wrapper is prompt craft only, holds no pictures, remembers nothing, publishes nothing, hideGalleryButtons: true); the two shapes - A, a thin wrapper with its own copies that ships in an afternoon and drifts within a month, and B, the wrapper owns the craft and this terminal imports it (craft = {import:lia-image-lane}) with studio.js becoming the UI over it, preferred and only on the day it is needed; the trigger (a second page that renders) with the five decisions that day needs (resolution and style, whether the veil travels, gating - this page has a door and somebody else's page has none unless it brings one - where the pictures live, and both flags); and the caveat worth deciding early: the tables are public only because src/ is public, and a standalone hosted copy of the veiled tongue is a far more findable thing than one file inside a large generator, so the veil travelling outside this tree is his call made deliberately rather than a side effect of shipping a wrapper. The file says plainly that it is a decision, not a task, so a later session does not helpfully build the thing. No code changed - not the studio, not the render path, not a command. AMENDED the same day, on his correction 'I am always logged in to perchance': the ad half of the cost argument was corrected in place - that ad is documented for the TEXT plugin in this generator's own main.pjs note, not measured for the image plugin, and it only appears for visitors who are not logged in, so a wrapper page only he opens pays nothing - and the request-allowance half was simply wrong, since it is per-user and a second page does not spend it twice. The drift argument, which was always the deciding one, is untouched.

NO NOISE. and whose section 2 is 'Voice is an input modality, not authority' (a spoken command establishes neither identity nor authority nor permission nor capability nor judgment nor agency - 'these concerns belong to other architectural components', which is exactly what the ECHO GUARD and the DIRECTIVES implement in text), and whose section 3 diagram names the family it sits in: COREPACK, AUTHPACK, GATEPACK, JUDGEPACK, FINPACK, GAMEPACK, LOREPACK. entries.title: THE FLUX HARVEST - EIGHT FREE IMAGE ROADS, A HUNDRED STYLES, AND A PICTURE THAT CHECKS ITSELF
entries.desc: Patrikios handed over mythos-flux-2026-09-27T04-38-34.zip (154,383 bytes: main.pjs 3,553, index.html 340,309 of which 251,994 is one classic script, src/ultra-worker.js 13,094, src/README.md 101,992) - a public free image generator - and asked for expert eyes on what is harvestable: 'This one allows for multiple image generators like flux, etc. Not saying we should, but the possibility exists, and there are features and elements I appreciate for the other modules. Like the 100 styles ready to go, etc.' Read: main.pjs in full, index.html's ~120 functions extracted and outlined, the worker in full, and the build's own 1,500-line README. NOTHING WAS BUILT and nothing changed in this tree - it is a reading. The archive is kept permanently at https://user.uploads.dev/file/65bb988e40176443bb6fb85a96c8badc.zip because the workspace copy is scratch and dies, and the harvest cites function and table names rather than line numbers so the receipts survive. THE FINDING: the interesting part of that generator is not its app - it is that it treats IMAGE SUPPLY as a table of eight roads behind one interface, and that it does not trust a picture until something has looked at it. (1) THE ENGINE INTERFACE: one declarative registry (HF_MODELS - key, name, tag, kind, host, api, minSide, stepsMin/Max, fixed dims, defaults) plus one runner per road with the same signature, (model, params, onEvent) -> [{url, mime}, seed], capability in the table and protocol in the runner, every road reporting process_starts/estimation/queue_size through the same event, so the panel is written once; this terminal's image lane has exactly ONE road. The roads, and which matter here: HORDE (Stable Horde) uses their documented anonymous key 0000000000, needs no signup, and asks nsfw true with censor_nsfw false so the prompt is NEVER REFUSED for its content - a shared community queue at anonymous priority and fixed 512x512 are the cost (over that the API demands kudos, translated to horde-kudos); that free keyless road that cannot refuse is the one failure this terminal's image lane actually has. ZEROCOST is Z-Image-Turbo from a shared GPU-token pool with its own daily allowance and is the only free road that also takes a negative prompt (token minting via get_token -> SSE -> success/token, zerocost-resting when the pool is dry); PERCHANCE (qinegen) is the very plugin this terminal already speaks to; PERCHANCEAISFW is the only safe-only road and the only one needing root.superFetch for both legs (428 proof-of-work, 429 paced); FLUXSCHNELL is FLUX.1 schnell at 4 steps; SDXLCPU is SDXL-Turbo on free CPU with NO daily limit at all (1-2 min, fixed 512x512); POLLINATIONS needs no key because the request IS the URL. And a cost decision in the house style: FLUX.1 dev and Krea were removed on request because 28 steps ate a whole visitor's daily allowance for one picture. (2) AUTO-VERIFY: verifyImage sends the finished picture back to the text model under a strict inspector prompt - judge only defects that make the picture look broken, never beauty, taste or style - with three defect lists (photograph / drawn, where it must never complain that anime is not a photo / general) chosen from the style group so a new variant is covered automatically (VERIFY_FAMILY_BY_GROUP); the answer is forced to one JSON line of ok/score/issues/avoid and verdictFromText refuses to believe ok true when it disagrees with the rest (any issue listed or a score under the pass mark means a defect whatever the boolean says); avoid is negative-prompt terms for the NEXT attempt, so the loop is render -> inspect -> re-render with the defects as negatives (generateVerified). This terminal already looks at pictures (renderVision) but does not score and re-roll - the difference between a description and a quality gate. (3) STYLES: about a hundred entries as key/name/phrase where the phrase is APPENDED to the prompt and never rewrites it, grouped into eight panel boxes (Basic / Realistic / Anime & Manga / Retro & Vintage / Painting & Art / 3D & CGI / Graphic & Design / Dark & Fantasy), and the clever part is the FORCED style - Realistic also strips contradictory style words (NON_REALISTIC_TERMS + stripNonRealisticTerms, segment by segment, dropping orphaned connectives so '3d render of a dragon' loses its 'of a' too) and adds a REALISM_NEGATIVE guard to the negative: a style that insists. The studio's recipe book is heavy craft; a style library is the cheap ninety percent. (4) THE WORKER: src/ultra-worker.js is tiled ESRGAN upscaling off the main thread as PRIMITIVES (open / aiPass / resample / sharpen / encode / close), plan and progress text decided on the page, OffscreenCanvas + ImageData instead of anything DOM, the model imported from esm.sh once and kept alive, 12 px tile context against seams, cooperative cancellation, and a main-thread mirror (ultraBackendMain) for when the worker cannot start - and underneath it the platform trap, in its own words: the worker is built from new URL('src/ultra-worker.js', location.href) and NOT from the document base URL, because perchance injects a base href tag pointing at perchance.org/<name> which would make the worker cross-origin. That is now a Gotchas bullet in src/README.md. (5) THREE SMALLER THINGS: the presence pill (a Set of connections, one pubsub topic and a count - the entire server plugin is 645 bytes, worth remembering the next time a server feature looks expensive); the error vocabulary (hfReadableError, isAbortError, horde-kudos, zerocost-resting, horde-timeout, 428/429 - each road's refusal translated into something actionable, and cancelling must never raise a page error); and prompt auto-translate (translatePromptText / ensureEnglish), relevant because he writes in Greek, plus the share loop whose dynamic(inputs) titles a shared link with the prompt it carries and browser-only local accounts - not for this terminal, but directly relevant to the public shelf of the artpack build. WHAT NOT TO TAKE: THE REDIRECT FUNNEL (window.__uaiConfig) bounces a first visit and every finished picture to a blogspot offer page, tried on the top frame then this frame, both via location.replace() so Back cannot undo the trip; both switches are OFF in the snapshot but the machinery is there - it is traffic monetization for a public generator and the recommendation is NOT PORTED, EVER; and the 252 KB single-script monolith, which has nothing this tree has not done better with one file per job. OPEN FOR HIM: whether to add the uncensored road as a second engine, whether to adopt the verify loop for renderVision, whether to add a style library beside the recipe book, and whether to take the worker upscale off the main thread.

entries.title: THE SIX ADVANCED SETTINGS - READ, MAPPED, AND RULED OUT OF THIS TERMINAL
entries.desc: The ask was to keep looking at the flux generator's Advanced panel and turn items 1-6 into a concrete change plan - file by file, with the switch names - before anything was built; the plan was written, and then ruled on the same day. HIS WORDS, the ruling: 'Let's leave it alone for here. It belongs in a dedicated art shop. We have enough for now. Save to your note on what we may decide to add in the future. We already have a working generator, why bother re-inventing the wheel? Let's leave it alone for now. She doesn;t need all the extra toys for now, She has huges pipes stuffing her asshole lol'. WHAT THE SIX WERE (index.html:1086-1222 in the archived source, in order): Resolution (#resSelect -> settings.resolution, with an 'auto' derived from the aspect chips), Detail boost (#detailCb -> settings.detailBoost, a phrase appended by prompt family), Auto-verify (#verifyCb -> settings.verify, generate -> vision check -> keep the best, with the checker's avoid words handed to the next attempt as negatives and a check that cannot answer ACCEPTED, never a failure), Checking budget (#verifyBudgetSel -> settings.verifyBudgetMs, VERIFY_BUDGET_MS = 120000, the first candidate always runs and an in-flight generation is never cancelled), Reference image (#refFile + #refStrength -> settings.reference -> opts.referenceImage), and Ultra resolution (#ultraBlock, #ultraCb, #ultraTargetChips 1K/2K/4K/8K longest side, #ultraSharpen - real ESRGAN 2x passes in a worker, then an exact-target resample and a strip-wise unsharp, the result a Blob and never a data URL). THE MAP: 1 already exists here (LIA_IMAGE_RESOLUTION + the four IMAGE_SIZES chips + forge.resolution in kv lia_settings/image_form) and its 'auto' has nothing to derive from because these chips ARE the aspects; 2 would have been LIA_IMAGE_BOOST with a new src/studio/boosts.json, an append moved to the single choke point renderImageNow (today LIA_IMAGE_STYLE is applied in renderVision alone, src/js/images.js:1882, and the forge bypasses it) and a /boost door; 3 and 4 are one build - a new src/js/verify.js + src/studio/defects.json with LIA_VERIFY / LIA_VERIFY_BUDGET_MS / LIA_VERIFY_MAX_TRIES and /verify, hung on the choke point, spending about 570 tokens of his key per attempt - and every primitive already exists (lookBlob is a transient vision call on a Blob, src/js/images.js:1944; the house negative default is the negative road; src/js/progress.js draws counted jobs); 5 must NEVER be built, and that is not a judgement call: imports/text-to-image-plugin/main.pjs:547 says in the plugin's own words that referenceImage 'is deliberately DISABLED server-side and currently has NO EFFECT on the generated output - the parameter is parsed and sent but ignored for general traffic (2026-08-25, per the platform owner). Don't build img2img flows on it', so flux's reference row is a dead control and a future session must not add it back 'because it is missing'; 6 is two separable things - a target SIZE (LIA_UPSCALE_LOCAL_TARGET + /upscale target 1k|2k|4k|8k) over a pipeline that already exists (bigger.pics 4x by window under src/js/pipeline.js, this machine in src/js/upscale-local.js), and the only genuinely new capability in the whole list, real AI super-resolution (LIA_UPSCALE_AI* + a new src/workers/ultra-worker.js + /upscale ai), which the local road does not have because it resamples and invents no detail. WHY NOT HERE: these six tune a stranger's one-off prompt on a public page, and this terminal already answers both halves of that question with craft (recipe book, pose book, shot list, veiled tongue, house negative) and with the pipeline; MYTHOS FLUX is the art shop and they belong beside its eight roads and style library, not inside a private terminal. WHAT WAS RECORDED AND WHERE: the full note is src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-six-advanced-settings.md, the pointer and the table are section 1dl of src/TODO.md, and the archived source is kept permanently at https://user.uploads.dev/file/65bb988e40176443bb6fb85a96c8badc.zip (Advanced panel at index.html:1086-1222) because the workspace copy was scratch and dies with its session. THE ONE THING THAT STAYS TRUE EITHER WAY: hideGalleryButtons: true lives at the choke point (renderImageNow, the only root.generateImage call site in the tree), so any future render road here - a verify loop included, if it is ever wanted - inherits never-public without anyone having to remember it. NO CODE CHANGED: not the image lane, not a command, not a single knob. AND THEN, HANDED THE MAP, THE ONE INSTRUCTION THAT SURVIVED THE WHOLE EXERCISE: 'Only this have value: Remove all odd fonts and emojis and perhaps find a logical place for them so they can be accessed during the create image operation.' Read as the one thing that survives, and as aimed at the ART SHOP rather than at this terminal. MEASURED, in the archived flux index.html (338,875 B): 250 emoji glyphs across 48 distinct symbols sit in the chrome and on the controls - Style, Advanced settings, Ultra resolution, Auto-verify, Free cloud models, My gallery, History, Login, Negative prompt, More quota, the engine names (qinegen, Z-Image, the safe-only engine) and the whole share row - and an emoji inside a monochrome label is drawn by the system's own emoji font, which is the 'odd font': a coloured glyph wearing a different typeface from the words beside it. Under it is the second oddity, labels at 9.5 / 11 / 12 / 13 px in three weights, uppercase and letter-spaced, so the chrome has no single voice. THE SECOND HALF IS THE PLACEMENT: the controls those emoji are stuck to should not be scattered over headers, modals and collapsed drawers - they belong in the create-image flow itself, one plain label each, reachable while a picture is made. AND HERE, MEASURED, THERE IS NOTHING TO STRIP: index.html 0 emoji, src/js/images.js 0, main.pjs 6 (three dice, one clapper, two arrows), src/css/terminal.css 3, src/js/forge.js 2 - so the ruling is a rule for anything adopted from flux (no emoji, no display fonts, no micro-type, one plain label per control, and the control lives where the creating happens) rather than a change to this tree.

entries.title: THE RECORD AT 5.87 MB - AND THE TWO THIRDS THAT LOST THEIR TURN NUMBERS
entries.desc: He pasted the CHATLOG panel's own index - the size, the thirty chunk rows, the import history, the join - with no words over it. Treated as a capture: read it, check it against the record itself, then say what it means. VERIFIED LIVE, not taken on trust: /chatlog listText() in the live page is byte-identical to the paste, and the record's own keys were read directly - chars 5,837,854 / bytes 6,155,234 / 109,534 lines / 30 chunks / turns 11,024 with indexed 'turns' / 11,024 rows in chatlog_marks / 17 rows in chatlog_meta.history / 1 join ('NOTHING OF THE RECORD WAS FOUND IN THE NEW FILE', so the whole file was appended after a marked join) / origin 60a6e23d828a54dc4c8b315f33c97ba3.perchance.org, name 2hoy6c5u0x. The newest import is the 2026-09-26 23:08:21 append of +2,156,996 characters from LIA-CHATLOG-20260926-2306.JSON, and the record's fingerprint is 7dda2dc0-59141e. THE COLUMN THAT MATTERS IN THE PASTE READ '0': chunks 1-18 and 30 carry no turns at all, and chunks 19-29 carry 644 / 1,213 / 1,126 / 947 / 1,350 / 1,255 / 1,307 / 1,226 / 764 / 729 / 463. FINDING 1 - THE INDEX STOPS AT THE SEAM, and the code says why: in put() (src/js/chatlog.js) the record's own marks are carried forward ONLY when the arriving file carries no turn list ('if (!(turns && turns.length) && old.indexed === "turns" && marks.length)'), and the last import was a .json sidecar - a real message list - so the carry never ran and the index was rebuilt from that list alone: 11,024 turns, all of them inside the newest 2.15 MB. The older 3.68 MB is still there and still searchable (/chatlog grep, /chatlog show) but no longer addressable by number - /chatlog turn <N> and /chatlog turns cannot reach any turn before the seam - so the import that made the record longer is the import that took the turn numbers off its first two thirds. Not a cap: LIA_CHATLOG_MARKS is 25,000 and only 11,024 are held. FINDING 2 - THE TAIL IS NOT A TURN: ENDS :: 'ERROR: MESSAGE TOO LONG, 78,797/64,000 CHARACTERS - DELIVERY IS UNKNOWN', the editor's own refusal stored verbatim and quoted by the BRIEF, because that is how the conversation the last import carried ended. WHAT WAS DONE, prose only: src/chatlog/README.md (the stale 'the record is three megabytes' is now the measured figure with its date, and the BRIEF's field list gained the tail bullet), src/README.md (THE CHATLOG - the carry-forward paragraph now states the asymmetry with the measurement and points at §1dm), src/TODO.md (§1dm). STILL OPEN, AND WAITING FOR HIS WORD: extend the turn index over the whole record - the road exists in the module already (LIA_CHATLOG_SPEAKER, markUp, turnsFromLines), but rebuilding chatlog_marks means writing to the record's own index in kv, which is his data, so nothing was run against the record: it was read only.

entries.title: CODY'S RULES - THE AGENT'S OWN LANE GETS A NAME AND A HOME
entries.desc: He had just read the agent's own account of reading the record - the brief, the record's first lines, and the entry explaining that lane - and answered with three words and a colon: 'Cody's Rules: Brief first, grep before re-deriving, write every pass down.' Taken as a designation: the rules ARE those three, his naming of them, and they belong where a later session will meet them rather than in a chat window that closes. WHAT WAS BUILT: src/cody/README.md, the agent's own lane - each rule with the door it is used through and the cost it exists to prevent. (1) BRIEF FIRST: /chatlog brief, two chunk reads whatever the record weighs, then /chronicle newest and the top of README.md - because a session that reads 5.87 MB whole spends itself on the reading, one that reads none of it re-derives settled ground, and where a session has been is not recoverable from the code at all; the honest caveat is written in rather than hidden - the brief's WHERE IT STARTS prints turn 1 of the IMPORTED region, not the conversation's first message (the index stops at the seam, TODO section 1dm), so show first is the true beginning until that is fixed. (2) GREP BEFORE RE-DERIVING: /chatlog grep, /docs search, /docs related, /renders find, /recipe negative, /lore, and grep before read in the file tools - because nearly every question has already been answered here, and the answer in the record is stronger than a memory of it since it carries the words and the date; a dead end that is not looked up gets walked again, a measurement gets guessed at, a ruling gets relitigated. (3) WRITE EVERY PASS DOWN: README (what is true now), TODO (one numbered section per pass), src/chronicle/ plus chronicle.json and src/pack/files.json, and src/rtfm/ whenever a command changed, then the check - rtfm.check() empty, the chronicle count, files equal to the tree - because the next session is not this one, and this project's chat window has already died once (the editor refused a 78,797-character message and the working context was compacted to a handoff). WHY A FIFTH LANE: src/lorepack/ is hers, src/rtfm/ is his manual, README+TODO are the state, src/chronicle/ is the making, and src/cody/ is the MAKER'S - how the building is done, by the agent doing it; not indexed, not retrieved, never handed to her, and public on purpose, because a rule a stranger can read is a rule a later session cannot quietly reinterpret. The lane table in src/chronicle/README.md went from four rows to five and its heading lost the word 'four'. WHAT WAS THOUGHT: a named rule is a rule that can be invoked - 'read the brief first' is advice, 'per Cody's Rules' is a citation; the chronicle entry of 2026-09-26 had already named this lane as the agent's own ('the memory of the agent that is doing the making, portable across his generators'), and he has now given it its first content and its first word; nothing was invented - the rules are his sentence, hung on doors that already exist. STILL OPEN: the rest of the pack he named on 2026-09-26 and which is still design (the records layer of decisions, lessons, facts and open items; the vocabulary file; the where query across projects; the portable container) - brief is its first primitive and lives in the chatlog, and src/cody/ is where the rest lands when he says so.

entries.title: THE AUDIONOOK IDEAS, HALF ONE - A LOCAL ENGINE FOR MORE FEMALE VOICES
entries.desc: he sent perchance.org/mythos-auto-gallery - the audiobook reader whose voice is KOKORO - with 'more female voice choices (maybe)', and it was answered with a measurement rather than an opinion: kokoro is an 82M ONNX model that runs locally and carries 28 English voices of which 15 are female, with the provider's own grades (Heart A, Bella A-, and thirteen lower). entries.title: THE PAIR ROAD - A THIRD ROAD BETWEEN DEVICES
entries.desc: his second idea under the same link, 'Device Synch', became the third road between machines: a 12-character code (alphabet with no I, L, O, 0 or 1) that one device shows and the other types, from which both derive the same room name (SHA-256 of a version prefix plus the code) and the same AES-GCM-256 key (PBKDF2, 200,000 rounds) - so the code is the only thing he carries, the room name is the only thing the server is told, and the key is transmitted by nobody. WHAT WAS BUILT: a stateless relay as the first server-plugin script in index.html (subscribe/publish fan-out, pair_join/leave/count/alive/ping, a 60/s token bucket, a 24,000-character frame cap, and state never touched - the whole element is public source, and nothing secret is in it); src/js/pair.js with the codec, the socket, and /pair status|new|join|open|close|send|name|log|forget|help; #pairBadge beside SYNC; and a commands.json entry. The payload is gzipped then sealed in ~9KB pieces, reassembled and digest-checked at the far end, and merged with the SAME merger /sync down uses, so it only ADDS or FILLS and can never delete. TWO BUGS CAUGHT BY TESTING: the first codec round-tripped ciphertext through a latin1 STRING (would have corrupted any compressed data) and an RPC reply ('ok' + unit separator + '2') was read as a peer, inventing a phantom device - both fixed, both proven by the run. VERIFIED in the unsaved emulator: ping/pong, a code, a second socket, presence showing exactly one peer, a 1000-turn archive (351KB compressed from 1303KB) sent in 40 sealed frames in about 2 seconds, digest matched, merged with zero kv writes when the far end already held it, then close and forget. THE HONEST COSTS: both devices must be open at once (no offline delivery, because there is no far-side storage on purpose) and the bulk rides the relay, where Audionook's own design uses a WebRTC side-channel - the trade buys a server that holds nothing.

entries.title: THE VOX PANEL AND THE BOARD - EVERY VOICE IN ONE PLACE, AND THE COMMAND THAT WAS NEVER WIRED
entries.desc: three asks in one message, and one ruling: a VOX button that walks every voice the terminal can speak with (this machine's own list, the wire's thirty, the local model's roster, the ElevenLabs account) with HEAR and KEEP for a chosen target - THE DEFAULT or the agent ON STAGE - and, on the only two roads that hand back real audio (kokoro returns a WAV, ElevenLabs an mp3), a SAMPLE verb that makes a CLIP out of a voice, files it in the VOX tree under the agent it is for, and sets it as what the story lane clones that agent from. WHAT WAS THOUGHT: the four roads are not equal and the panel must not pretend they are - the Web Speech API exposes no audio to capture and the wire's voices exist inside a live socket, so SAMPLE is ABSENT on those two rows and the reason is written at the foot of the panel, because a button that cannot work is a lie with a cursor; the panel is a FRONT-END on purpose (voice.voxRoster and voice.voxSet, so KEEP and the matching /voice verb are the same act and there is no fifth copy of how a road works); and mint() in voice.js is the one road between the voice lane and the story lane. THE BOARD: the other generator's device-sync screen, copied in shape and NOT in one detail - Patrikios ruled 'To be clear, no invite links. We remain private.' - so the pair lamp became a button onto #pairPanel: the code read off one screen and typed into the other, COPY THE CODE (the code, not a link), REJOIN, SYNC NOW, and STOP SYNCING THIS DEVICE behind an arm-then-press; and THE GROUP FINGERPRINT, which is DERIVED and not stored - the first sixteen characters of the room's name, the SHA-256 of the code, which each device computes for itself, so 'it must read the same on every device' is a consequence rather than a promise, and a mismatch is visible at a glance. VERIFIED LIVE: 70 rows across four roads; the clone sample made a real 399,644-byte 24kHz WAV in 8.3s, filed as 'Heart sample.wav' in /audio/vox with tags [sample, kokoro], and set through story.setSample (the test record was then deleted and the fallback restored, so nothing of the test remains); the fingerprint recomputed independently from the code matched the panel exactly; a simulated second device made the board say 'IN A ROOM WITH 1 OTHER DEVICE', enabled SYNC NOW, and received 43 sealed frames (~488KB); STOP SYNCING THIS DEVICE left the code, the room and the run record off the device. WHAT WENT WRONG, and it is the finding of the session: /pair HAD NEVER BEEN REACHABLE BY TYPING - declared in commands.json with no dispatch block in chat.js, so a typed /pair was answered with the message reserved for a TYPO, and every earlier test had called pair.run() directly instead of through its door. Both /pair and /vox are dispatched now and verified through the input box. AND A MEASUREMENT ABOUT HIS VAULT, taken while cleaning up: 189 records, 180 pictures and 9 clips and ZERO audio - the VOX tree exists and is empty, the fifty-one clips filed there by hand are gone from this browser, and the story lane's sample for BARBELO still names a clip the vault cannot produce. STILL OPEN: whether to re-make the samples with the new road, a real look at the two panels on his screen (the page-snapshot helper hangs even on a single element in this preview, so the check was geometric), and ElevenLabs previews billing a credit per character.

entries.title: THE TAGS - MALE OR FEMALE, AND ONLY WHERE IT IS KNOWN
entries.desc: Patrikios: 'For the moment, I ask that the available voices be TAGGED - Male or Female - in the VOX system.' WHAT WAS BUILT: every VOX row now carries a chip - F in pink, M in blue - with a per-road tally in each road's header (F 6 · M 6 · UNTAGGED 16), a SEX :: line in /vox, a legend at the foot of the panel and an F n · M n count in the state line; the rule is voice.sexOf(name, hint) in src/js/voice.js, the name table is src/voice/voices.json -> sex (a note and 217 names), .vxSex in src/css/terminal.css is the only colour in the panel, the vox entry in commands.json carries the rule, and src/rtfm/commands.md was regenerated (82 commands, /rtfm check clean). WHAT WAS THOUGHT: a tag must be a claim the terminal can stand behind - the local model's roster carries gender for every voice and the ElevenLabs palette states it in each voice's note (an account's list carries it in labels.gender), so those tags are the provider's own word and nothing is guessed; this browser's list and the live wire publish NO such field, so there the NAME is read against the table and the chip's own title says the tag is INFERENCE, not measurement; and a missing chip is an answer, not a hole - 16 browser voices (the generic Google language voices) and 14 wire voices (the star-named ones) are left blank rather than guessed, because a wrong tag is worse than an empty one, and River is deliberately absent from the table because it is female in the local model and 'neutral' at ElevenLabs, so a single name key would lie about one of them. MEASURED (this machine): THE LOCAL VOICE 28 = 15 F / 13 M / 0 untagged, ELEVENLABS 12 = 6 F / 5 M / 1, THIS BROWSER 28 = 6 F / 6 M / 16, THE WIRE 30 = 8 F / 8 M / 14; panel totals with all four roads loaded: 98 voices, 35 F, 32 M, 31 untagged; and the chips were checked at 1600x900 and 390x844 with no row overflow and every chip inside its row - geometric, not a picture, because the page-snapshot helper still hangs in this preview. WHAT WENT WRONG, and it is the lesson of the pass: design() returns a WHITELIST of the design file's fields, so the brand-new sex block never reached sexMap() and the table was always empty while the name-regex path worked perfectly - found by printing what sexOf returned for known names and by fetching the served JSON to prove the file itself was right, and fixed with one line (sex: (cfg && cfg.sex) || null in defaults()). The same message carried his larger direction - custom voice and TTS without paying ElevenLabs forever, the captured audio of the default persona voice and native Greek speakers used today for ChatterBox and longform, the nook reader as an audiobook maker, myths from the LOREPACK saved to the Sacred Archive as audio, and her 'time off' creative work - which is RECORDED, not built (README, TODO 1dr); and the voice he thought he had not sent is on file at elevenlabs.profiles.lia (0oYUKTNPbymIKVAkDQqh, refused on a free plan with HTTP 402). AND, HALFWAY THROUGH THE PASS, THE ORIGIN MOVED: the generator was renamed 2hoy6c5u0x -> mythos-lia-barbelo, the window.generatorPublicId went 60a6e23d... -> 7f77c07f..., and the subdomain with it - so on the new origin the terminal is EMPTY (kv lia_settings down to folders + sync, the vault measured at 0 records / 0 bytes where the previous session measured 189, the door's answer and the story samples with them), while getGeneratorStats?name=2hoy6c5u0x now answers generator-does-not-exist and the new name carries the generator and its $meta intact: a rename, not a fork, with the ID moving with the NAME. The house had believed the opposite in writing ('A RENAME is also free - the name is the path, the ID is the origin'), so the old claim and a dated correction are now both in src/TODO.md, and the finding is recorded in TODO 1dr ('A FINDING THAT IS NOT CODE: THE ORIGIN MOVED'). Nothing in the pass caused it and the agent renamed nothing; the data is on the other subdomain and the name is the key back to it.

entries.title: THE GATEKEEPER - ACCESS OR DENY BEFORE THE AGE SCREEN
